#3107. Top Wall Street analysts prefer these dividend stocks for boosting portfolio returns

Dividend stocks remain a popular choice for investors seeking steady income and higher portfolio returns. However, with thousands of dividend-paying companies to choose from, identifying the right stocks can be challenging.

In this regard, recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can provide useful insights and help identify dividend stocks backed by solid fundamentals and with attractive upside potential.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Recently, Evercore analyst Chris Baker initiated coverage of Permian Resources stock with a price target of $25. The analyst believes that the company is well positioned to benefit from improving U.S. shale demand after the Iran conflict, thanks to its low-breakeven inventory that can boost free cash flow growth. Baker also noted PR's disciplined consolidation in the Permian Basin.

Furthermore, the 5-star analyst highlighted the company's focus on a single basin and management's efficient capital allocations across expansion efforts, strategic acquisitions, and share buybacks. Baker noted that management focuses investments on the higher-return Northern Delaware Basin, helping boost profitability.

"The key piece of our work here, and the reason we think PR deserves a higher multiple relative to more finite or less flexible shale stories, is that PR runs an acquire and exploit model," said Baker.

He explained that Permian Resources deserves a premium valuation as it continually acquires and develops new high-quality assets instead of relying on a limited inventory, a strategy that is the market is underappreciating.

Baker ranks No. 862 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 48.3%. See Permian Resources Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Valero Energy (VLO) is a manufacturer and marketer of petroleum-based and low-carbon liquid transportation fuels and petrochemical products. At a quarterly dividend of $1.20 per share, or annualized dividend of $4.80 per share, VLO stock offers a yield of about 2%.

Heading into Valero's second-quarter earnings on July 30, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on VLO stock and increased the price target to $286 from $283 to reflect updated estimates.

Specifically, the 5-star analyst raised his 2026 and 2027 earnings per share estimates to $31.42 and $23.07 from $29.42 and $21.06, respectively, while leaving the 2028 EPS estimate unchanged at $20.37. Mehta made these revisions based on several factors, including updated commodity price assumptions and changes to refining capture rates.

Despite a strong year-to-date rally in VLO stock, Mehta still finds it compelling due to his more positive refining outlook. Moreover, the analyst sees the possibility of solid estimate revisions, which could drive the stock higher. He believes that Valero is well-positioned to benefit from improving refining market conditions due to its strong position in the Gulf Coast, solid balance sheet strength, and low-cost operations.

"Additionally, we believe the company's premium asset portfolio and crude slate optionality should support capture rates and stronger cash flow generation in the near-term, ultimately supporting shareholder returns," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 742 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.2%. See Valero Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Ovintiv (OVV), a North American oil and natural gas producer. It has solid positions in North America's premier oil basins – the Permian and the Montney. OVV offers a quarterly dividend of 30 cents per share, or an annualized dividend of $1.20 per share, implying a 2.3% yield.

Following meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Gregory Pardy reaffirmed a buy rating on Ovintiv stock with a price target of $70, highlighting that the stock is on RBC's Global Energy Best Ideas List.

"In our eyes, the depth of Ovintiv's Montney position, streamlined portfolio, strong balance sheet and enhanced shareholder returns afford investors with an attractive valuation re-rating opportunity over time," said Pardy.

The 5-star analyst stated that his meetings with management bolstered his confidence in the company's outlook and potential to achieve a higher valuation. Pardy noted Ovintiv's transformation, with the company streamlining its portfolio from six basins (including the Uinta, Bakken and Anadarko) to two – the Montney and Permian – while enhancing the depth of its inventory.

Pardy also emphasized OVV's improved shareholder returns and solid balance sheet following the recent sale of its assets in the Anadarko Basin for $3 billion.

Pardy ranks No. 169 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 22.3%. See Ovintiv Options Trading Activity on TipRanks.

#3106. Auna (AUNA) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Colombian oncology costs weighed on profits, but cash flow surged.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 18, 2026 at 4:08PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Auna (AUNA -12.37%) reported top-line growth driven by higher surgical volumes and oncology sessions across its regional platform, though consolidated profitability was impacted by extraordinary costs in Colombia and Peru. Management reported that the company terminated an unprofitable oncology risk-sharing contract in Colombia that represented 4% of segment revenue after treatment costs significantly exceeded assumptions. In Mexico, the Monterrey healthcare network achieved its first quarter of Adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026, offsetting regulatory changes in VAT deductibility that affected the insurance sector. The company reported substantial year-to-date free cash flow growth of 95%, which supported a reduction in the net leverage ratio to 3.5x. Management reaffirmed its full-year revenue guidance of 10% to 14% growth while revising Adjusted EBITDA expectations to remain broadly stable or slightly down for the year.

Operator: Good morning, and welcome to Auna's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. My name is Alexandra, and I will be the operator for today's call. [Operator Instructions] And please note that this call is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] Now I would like to turn the call over to Ana Maria Mora, Head of Investor Relations. Ma'am, please go ahead.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, operator. Hello, everyone, and welcome to Auna's conference call to review our third quarter results. Please note that there is a webcast presentation to accompany the discussion during this call. If you need a copy of the presentation, please go to our Investor Relations website or contact Auna's Investor Relations team. Please note that when we discuss variances, we will be doing so on a year-over-year basis and in FX-neutral or local currency terms with regard to Mexico and Colombia, unless we note otherwise. Let's move to Slide 2. In addition to reporting unaudited financial results in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards, we will discuss certain non-IFRS financial measures and operating metrics, including foreign exchange neutral calculations.

Investors should carefully read the definitions of these measures, the metrics and reconciliations included in our earnings press release published yesterday after market close to ensure that they understand them. Non-IFRS financial measures and operating metrics should not be considered in isolation as a substitute for or superior to IFRS financial measures and are provided as supplemental information only. Before we begin our remarks, please also note that certain statements made during the course of today's discussion may constitute forward-looking statements, which are based on management's current expectations and beliefs and which are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to materially differ, including factors that may be beyond the company's control.

These include, but are not limited to, our revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure guidance, our target leverage ratio, the results of the key initiatives we are implementing in Mexico, Colombia and Peru, the timeline for the construction and commencement of operations at Centro Ambulatorio Trecca, the expected capacity and market of Centro Ambulatorio Trecca once built, our ability to recover any loss under the oncology risk-sharing contract in Colombia, the execution of our strategic plan, our planned investments, our expected revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA growth, the expected impact of regulatory price caps in Colombia and the creation of further growth and sustainable value for all stakeholders.

For a description of risks that may impact our forward-looking statements, please refer to our Form 20-F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and our earnings press release. Slide 3, please. On today's call, we have Jesus Zamora, our Executive Chairman and President; Gisele Remy, our Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President; and Lorenzo Massart, our Executive Vice President of Strategy and Equity Capital Markets. They will discuss Auna's consolidated and segment financial and operating results for the quarter as well as provide an update on our various strategic growth initiatives. After that, we will open the call for your questions. Jesus, please go ahead.

Jesús Zamora Leon: Thank you, Annie. Let's begin with Slide 4, please. We maintained our growth momentum across Auna's regional platform in the third quarter, delivering top-line growth of 10% on an FX-neutral basis. Particularly encouraging was the acceleration of growth in Mexico with improving profitability and its first quarter of year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth in 2026 and the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. In Colombia, profitability was pressured by significant medical costs under specific oncology risk-sharing contract and drug pricing caps. Importantly, the underlying business continued to demonstrate strong momentum, delivering a third consecutive quarter of robust revenue growth, supported by increased high-complexity care.

We took decisive action to address the situation, and we'll discuss this particular contract in more detail in today's presentation. Third quarter profitability was also impacted by penalties related to the reconciliation of prior years' receivables in Peru. The underlying strength and growth potential of our Peru segment remain intact, and we continue to see significant opportunities from our strategic focus on high-complexity care and other growth initiatives in this market. We sustained strong cash generation, driven by disciplined working capital management and improved cash conversion, directly supporting our ongoing deleveraging efforts. Let's move to Slide 5.

Our third consecutive quarter of strong revenue growth and a 95% year-over-year increase in year-to-date free cash flow demonstrate the continued strength of our platform's fundamentals. This robust cash generation supported a sequential improvement in our leverage ratio to 3.5x, bringing us closer to our medium-term target of 3x. This underlying strength is also reflected in the operating metrics at the bottom of this slide. Total capacity utilization in our healthcare services network increased year-over-year to 68% on a year-to-date basis, reflecting continued improvement in utilization across our platform. In Mexico, total capacity utilization increased 2 percentage points year-over-year during the quarter. In Peru, total plan memberships continue to grow and Oncosalud's oncology MLR stood at 50.7%.

These trends, together with the quarterly operating metrics we published last month, reinforce our confidence in our integrated healthcare model and the AunaWay. We remain confident in the medium- to long-term potential of our increasingly scaled and integrated regional platform. Let's move to Slide 7 for a closer look at our performance in Mexico. Driving the acceleration of Mexico's top line and the recovery in profitability were increases in surgery volumes, up 12% year-over-year as well as chemotherapy and radiotherapy sessions, which increased 34%. These trends demonstrate that the AunaWay and our strategy continues to gain traction in Mexico, a key market for Auna's long-term growth.

While our insurance business in Mexico navigated industry-wide headwinds from the new VAT deductibility regulations, the strength and volume growth of our Monterrey Healthcare network more than offset those impacts, allowing Mexico's segment Adjusted EBITDA to return to year-over-year growth. Despite the VAT's impact on Mexico's insurance market, we remain excited about the opportunities in the B2B segment through Auna Seguros, building on our established position and effective sales channels in dental and vision insurance. Moreover, our thesis on the long-term potential of oncology insurance in Mexico has not changed. We see significant opportunities to develop this product, further strengthen Auna's vertical integration and expand access to our value-based care model in this market. Slide 8, please.

Driving Peru's top-line growth was a 21% increase in surgery volumes, along with an 18% increase in chemotherapy and radiotherapy sessions as we further prioritize high-complexity procedures across our healthcare network. Another driver was our greater focus on higher retention B2B accounts through Oncosalud's multichannel access model. By way of example, we expect to onboard approximately 4,000 additional plan members in the fourth quarter following the signing of 2 new corporate agreements. The onboarding of new B2B accounts, which have yet to reach normalized utilization levels, together with higher pharmacy and clinical payroll expenses associated with increased hospitalization and emergency volumes weighed on Peru's profitability during the quarter.

Results were also affected by the penalties related to the reconciliation of prior years' receivables. These factors contributed to a 6% decline in consolidated Peru Adjusted EBITDA. Excluding the billing-related penalties, Adjusted EBITDA would have remained broadly stable year-over-year. Let's turn to Slide 9. The underlying fundamentals of our business in Colombia remained strong. As announced last quarter, we expanded our ICU and hospitalization capacity at IMAT Oncomédica in Montería to support growing demand for high-complexity care. Additionally, we further diversified our payor base, increasing revenues from private payors while further reducing our exposure to government-intervened payors. While we delivered a 12% increase in Colombia's revenues in local currency, segment Adjusted EBITDA declined 30%, primarily reflecting 2 factors.

First, extraordinary adverse medical costs under a specific oncology risk-sharing contract, representing approximately 4% of Colombia's revenues. This contract covered approximately 500,000 lives and experienced a significantly higher incidence of advanced-stage cancer cases than anticipated, resulting in treatment costs that significantly exceeded contractual assumptions. We have since terminated this contract to limit further exposure and have engaged legal counsel to review all recovery options under the contract. Second, regulatory price caps enacted since mid-August impacted the third quarter and will continue to carry an impact in the fourth quarter as we implement the operational changes to contain this cost increase.

Inflationary pressures such as high personnel costs, reflecting mandatory wage increases and the statutory reduction in the standard workweek already discussed in previous quarters continued to weigh on our Colombian operations. To mitigate the impact of these pressures, we continue to focus on actively managing our revenue mix and payor portfolio as well as initiatives to improve operating efficiency across our Colombian network with the objective of recovering our structural margins. While these headwinds have affected our near-term results, our priority remains strengthening contract economics and building on the growth opportunities across our Colombian healthcare network. I'll now turn the call over to Gisele, who will review our results in more detail.

Gisele Ferrero: Thanks, Jesus, and good morning, everyone. Let's now turn to Slide 11, please. Our strategic focus on delivering more high-complexity services and value-based care continued driving revenue growth across our regional platform during the third quarter. In Mexico, the 12% increase in surgery volumes and 34% increase in oncology services drove a 2.9 percentage point increase in total capacity utilization, which rose to 41%. In Peru, where Auna is vertically integrated, surgeries grew an impressive 21%, while average monthly revenue per membership plan increased 5%, reflecting our successful strategy to onboard high-quality corporate B2B accounts, retain more profitable members and maintain disciplined pricing across our plans.

In Colombia, we continued capturing more growth in the private market with revenues from private payors increasing 22% in the quarter. Other growth drivers were the reactivation of ICU beds and the addition of hospitalization beds in Montería. Let's now move on to Adjusted EBITDA on Slide 12. As you can see in the bridge on this slide, our consolidated EBITDA reflects 3 distinct quantifiable drivers. First, on the positive side, Mexico achieved 5% year-on-year growth in Adjusted EBITDA, demonstrating the operating leverage we are beginning to capture in that market. Notably, the Monterrey healthcare network's Adjusted EBITDA increased 10% year-on-year, helping to mitigate soft results at Auna Seguros due to the sector-wide change in the deductibility of VAT.

However, this underlying growth was temporarily offset by 2 extraordinary items in Colombia and Peru. In Peru, our results absorbed PEN 18 million in revenue adjustments, primarily related to the prior years' billing matters. Excluding the net impact of these revenue adjustments, EBITDA would have been broadly stable year-over-year. As we've previously communicated, we have seen continued improvements in our internal billing cycle, helping to protect us from these types of impacts in future revenue billings that we generate. As such, we should be absorbing the majority of these impacts in the coming quarters, paving the way for Peru's EBITDA margins to recover towards their historical levels in the low 20s.

In Colombia, our results were impacted by the previously mentioned specific oncology risk-sharing contract, where treatment costs significantly exceeded contractual assumptions as well as new regulatory price caps on high-cost oncology medicines. We have successfully terminated this unprofitable contract, which represented approximately 4% of Colombia's revenue, effectively eliminating this near-term headwind. Additionally, it is important to note that the price caps only had a partial effect in the third quarter as they were implemented halfway through the period. Let's now move to Slide 13, please. Our Adjusted Net Income decreased versus the third quarter of 2025, driven by accounting effects rather than operational cash performance.

Specifically, the decrease reflects the absence of a PEN 40 million non-cash FX gain that we recorded in the same period last year. This is in line with what we have noted in previous quarters regarding the fact that following our most recent refinancing exercise in the fourth quarter 2025, we reset the levels on our FX hedges. Therefore, future FX variances should be very limited and should only occur when the U.S. dollar moves outside the 3.4 to 3.8 range. Our underlying net finance costs, when you strip out FX impacts as well as the non-cash impact of the future purchase obligation of IMAT Oncomédica, actually improved year-over-year.

Our current blended interest rate, including hedges and a majority of local currency funding, is at 10.38% year-to-date. The other significant and positive delta in the quarter was a PEN 20 million decrease in income tax expenses. Let's turn to cash flow on Slide 14, please. We continue to effectively increase cash conversion through improved collections as well as a reduced net tax payment across our platform. Year-to-date, net operating cash flow increased 62% to PEN 713 million, while free cash flow surged 95% to PEN 626 million.

This strong performance was driven by disciplined working capital management, specifically improved collections and lower accounts receivable days in Peru and Mexico as well as stable collections in Colombia, alongside lower tax payments. Over the 9-month period, our cash conversion cycle improved from negative 9 days in 2025 to negative 15 days, allowing us to continue generating cash through active working capital management. Year-to-date, our cash position increased 83% to PEN 614 million, keeping us on track to reach our medium-term leverage target of 3x. Lastly, at 3% of revenue, our CapEx remained comfortably below our 4% full-year guidance. Let's now move to our debt profile on Slide 15.

In addition to the slight improvement in net debt leverage resulting from Auna's increasing cash flow, it's important to note that our gross debt decreased by PEN 7 million on an FX-neutral basis, an improvement masked by the depreciation of the sol against the U.S. dollar, which resulted in an increase of PEN 90 million since year-end 2025. At the end of the third quarter, we had $194 million in credit lines, of which just over $134 million was still available for use. It's also important to note that 54% of our debt is in local currencies, while 85% of the balance in the U.S. dollar-denominated debt is hedged against the Peruvian sol.

In addition, 75% of our floating interest Mexican debt is also hedged. Finally, of the PEN 481 million of gross debt coming due in the next year, PEN 216 million corresponds to revolving working capital debt, which is renewed at maturity and which is amply covered by the USD 194 million in credit lines already mentioned. Additionally, PEN 165 million corresponds to the short-term maturities on our 2030 term loan and which is also amply covered by the PEN 614 million in cash balance at the close of the third quarter. The remainder corresponds to other short-term maturities of long-term borrowings as well as the accumulated interest on our outstanding 2029 and 2032 bonds. That concludes my review.

I'll now hand the call back to Jesus, who has a few closing remarks before we open the call for questions.

Jesús Zamora Leon: Thanks, Gisele. Consistent with the outlook communicated in October and in yesterday's earnings release, we continue to expect full-year 2026 revenue growth within our guidance range of 10% to 14% on an FX-neutral basis. Adjusted EBITDA is expected to remain broadly stable or slightly down year-over-year. This principally reflects the extraordinary medical costs associated with the terminated oncology contract in Colombia as well as the impact of regulatory price caps on certain high-cost oncology medications. Our capital expenditure guidance also remains unchanged at approximately 4% of consolidated revenues.

In Peru, where our integrated model has been operating at scale, we expect to capture the significant growth opportunities that remain in this market with a focus on expanding high-complexity services beyond oncology, including neurosurgery, traumatology and orthopedics as well as cardiovascular surgery. We expect profitability to improve as the onboarding of new B2B accounts normalizes. Mexico is now well positioned for sustained growth and improving profitability, supported by improved payor classifications, continued physician onboarding, the expansion of our oncology franchise and growing surgical volumes. Mexico has also maintained its growth momentum so far in the fourth quarter.

While we remain cautious on Colombia in the near term, given the regulatory and operating cost pressures discussed earlier, the market remains an integral part of our regional platform. We expect Colombia to gradually recover and once again become an important contributor to profitable growth, supported by the continued expansion of high-complexity care in Montería and our PGP arrangements. Finally, strong free cash flow generation enables us to further strengthen our balance sheet and make progress toward our medium-term leverage target of 3x. Before we open the call for questions, I want to emphasize that as we address these near-term headwinds, we remain confident in the long-term potential of our regional platform, our integrated care model and our market-specific strategies.

Our focus remains on accelerating growth in Mexico, restoring profitability in Colombia, improving earnings quality and operating efficiency in Peru and translating our commercial momentum to stronger cash generation and growing sustainable returns for our shareholders. Operator, please open the call for questions.

Mauricio Cepeda: We have 2 questions. The first one regarding Colombia. Gisele Ferrero: Yes. And thank you, Mauricio, for the question. Jesús Zamora Leon: Yes. Sorry, I forgot to unmute myself, so I was giving a very long-winded, but I'll try to summarize that. Thank you, Mauricio. Gisele Ferrero: Yes. Jesús Zamora Leon: Yes. And I would add that 80% of our payor relationships have confirmed the tiers in which we currently operate, which is a larger populations that are covered by insurance. Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Gisele. Give me 1 second. The next question comes from [indiscernible] and the question is, is there any negative impact expected on EBITDA margin for 4Q '26 due to the headwinds experienced in 3Q '26?

We will continue to see recovery of the Mexico business in the fourth quarter, and we will continue to see EBITDA growth into the fourth quarter of Mexico's EBITDA. Cash flow generation has improved significantly as we've been able to reduce the internal billing cycle and the cash flow conversion off the back of improved collections. Jesús Zamora Leon: Yes. And I would add, Gisele, that more directionally, I mean, 2026 has been -- and this quarter, in particular, has been about extraordinary unexpected impacts to our results. We need to continue to do what we've done for decades now to make sure that we have an affordable product that covers well the ailments, especially prevention and early detection and produces, of course, these high survival rates at an accessible price. I don't think there's any headwinds in particular, but small commercial actions that are required to continue to grow our covered population.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Gisele. And just to continue on the topic of Peru, there's another question from [indiscernible] and he's asking, with hospitals in Peru running at 90% utilization, how do you see volume growth potential from here?

Jesús Zamora Leon: Well, again, we're so focused on high complexity that sometimes the measurement of beds is not the most appropriate. And as you might have seen from what we have reported in the past, we're building a site in the south of Lima that addresses capacity utilization. And more importantly, we're doing more and more in high-complexity outpatient services. And I think that's a key strategic direction of how we build capacity. And I think some of the research analysts have always published our asset-light strategy. So we don't need to build these huge hospitals we have everywhere.

We can actually just marginally build asset-light facilities that can deliver services for hundreds of patients and family members a day without huge investments. And that's -- you will see us pushing that lever aggressively in -- particularly in Peru and Colombia.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Jesus. The next question...

Jesús Zamora Leon: Sorry, Annie, I'm sorry. I just want to make sure that we are comfortable. I forgot to respond this part. We're comfortable at 90% capacity utilization. We run our hospitals at those levels. And above that, it triggers an immediate need to act on the asset-light expansion, as I indicated before. I just wanted to make that point.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Jesus. To continue on the topic of Peru, there's a question -- a couple of questions from [indiscernible]. He's asking, when will the Peruvian billing issues wrap up? And then about Mexico, I understand that the VAT issues in Mexico will normalize because they affect everyone. Is that correct? Will there be diminished overall demand because of that? And finally, any news on the strategic MOU?

Jesús Zamora Leon: Okay. Let me tackle the second one, so that I can pass the mic to you, Gisele. So on VAT in Mexico, it should be read in a different light. Yes, it does affect everybody. It does affect everybody, but it actually gives a benefit to those of us that have a cost point for insurance payors that is most attractive. And that's why you see us grow. Yes, it does affect everybody. But we have a price point that's very attractive to insurance companies, and we're growing. I think we've continued to do that with the pressures of the insurance companies. And the first question was on Peru, and Gisele, on revenue reconciliation.

And the third question was on surges, I think, right?

Gisele Ferrero: Correct. Just quickly to tackle the Peru question on when we expect the billing issues in Peru to normalize. As I mentioned earlier, we have had very material improvements in the internal billing cycle. And as we've mentioned in previous quarters, we continue to negotiate reconciliations from previous periods, which is why we continue to have these effects being reflected in the coming quarters. We do expect to be able to reflect the effects related to previous periods within the next coming quarters and then be able to normalize those effects towards the second half of 2027.

Jesús Zamora Leon: And then on the Sojitz, we're making good progress. In relations with Sojitz, we think we should have something at the beginning of the year, perhaps to announce. We're excited about partnering with them and they have such a credible healthcare footprint elsewhere. But we're still early to talk much about it, but we are excited about that venture.

Ana Maria Mora: Okay. And then to continue on -- well, diverted from Peru, but I'd like to address Torre Trecca. [indiscernible] asked, could you explain the next steps regarding the Torre Trecca project?

Jesús Zamora Leon: So the good news is that the Torre Trecca project, the Centro Ambulatorio Trecca, is on schedule. I think it was a week ago or 2 weeks ago that we actually disbursed the first payment for construction. So -- and we had President Fujimori visiting the site less than 2 weeks ago as well. We had the Head of the EsSalud, the Social Security in Peru. So I think we're on time. And no, we don't see any surprises in the near future on that project. We're very excited. The government is very excited. I think we can make a huge difference as we have for other populations that we serve.

But it's a very important project, not because of the size of the project itself because it will prove Auna's capabilities in the B2G, B2 government sector, which, of course, in Mexico and Peru, in particular, is a high multiple, 5x, 6x of the private sector market. So we're really excited about this and what -- where this can take us in B2G and PPP projects in the region. Thank you very much for that question.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Jesus. And as we're getting to the final questions, there is a question about Mexico, and then we'll touch upon the El Niño. So about Mexico, this was from [indiscernible]. Could you give further color on how long the 16% revenue increase for the ISSSTELEON B2B agreement at OCA has impacted 3Q? And what would be in Mexico, excluding the aforementioned related revenue growth?

Gisele Ferrero: Okay. Yes. Thank you. As we've mentioned in previous quarters, 1 of the drivers for volume and margin recovery in 2026 have been related to the renewal of the ISSSTELEON contract towards the end of last year, beginning of this year at better conditions. So obviously, that has also had the effect of us taking in a higher amount of volume versus the comparable period of last year. And we will continue to see our B2G segment, as Jesus has mentioned, in the case of Mexico and specifically Monterrey, having a positive impact on our revenue mix, and it's a segment that we are very interested in growing also in the coming years.

Ana Maria Mora: Thank you, Gisele. And finally, the last question in the queue is about the phenomenon, El Niño potential and the impact. If you could discuss how we're going to support the infrastructure continuity and the medicine supply?

Gisele Ferrero: Yes. Thank you, Annie. And as we also mentioned in our Investor Day, the market has a forecast for a strong to extremely strong El Niño for the end of this year, beginning of next year, and weather can be highly unpredictable. So as a result, we've activated a plan that is dedicated to driving forward different actions in order to make sure that we have operational continuity and that we ensure the safety of our patients and our staff. In line with that, we are reinforcing infrastructures. We're ensuring critical supply for different medications and other kinds of supplies.

And we're making sure that we have backup supplies for fuel, water, electricity and our own generators, both backup generators, making sure that we have pre-organized flows for patients back and forth between where we need and also continuing to make sure that we have guaranteed flows between Northern Peru and Lima and between Arequipa and Lima. So we're doing this not only for Piura, Chiclayo and Trujillo, where probably most of the impact will happen, but also in Arequipa and Lima, so across our entire Peru network.

We're doing this as efficiently as possible, but again, making sure that we cover and make sure that our patients will be well taken care of and also ensuring the safety of our staff.

Ana Maria Mora: Okay. Thank you, Gisele. I think with that, we have reached the end of our question queue today. So thank you all for your time and participation. And Jesus, let me hand it back to you for some final thoughts.

Jesús Zamora Leon: Thank you, Annie. Before my final thoughts, I just wanted to add that we are as prepared as 1 can be for El Niño, better prepared than at any moment in the last decade that we have Niño. So we know what needs to be done. And we built a lot of cushions to make sure that our populations and our clinical staff is well protected for Niño events. I would like to also highlight, I'm not sure if this is appropriate for the call. We had a very important, I would say, blessed visit from the Pope these couple of days in Peru.

And we had the fortune to make sure that if anything occurred to him, he will be safe and healthy on the site by Auna. So we covered his visit with the Auna staff and the Auna ambulances. And I want to say that because that shows -- that should show the investor community the capabilities we have to sustain a service offering that is unique, that is unique. El Niño is unique. The visit to the Pope is unique. There were some masses that had 2 million people. And I think that should give the investor community another indicator of how we operate. Now in terms of my closing remarks, I want to be very clear.

It's been a tough quarter. It's been a very tough quarter. Colombia is, of course, concerning, but we're on it. And I want to make it very clear, we're on it. We have a great team led by Rayet Harb, that gives me comfort. We will turn the page on the current challenges. And Mexico and Peru are on the right track and gaining momentum. So we're very enthused about that. We want to thank you for the support. Thank you for your attention. And with that, I'd like to close the session. Thank you very much.

Operator: This concludes today's conference. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

#3105. Zane Lowe shares Apple Music Radio audience numbers, recalls ‘crickets’ in the early days

In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:

We were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The issue of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift…

#3102. Nvidia's Board Chairman Says Jensen Huang Isn't Coming Back, but He May Have a Poker Move for the Ages Hiding up His Sleeve

Nvidia's Board Chair, Harvey Jones, says the company does not plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 18, 2026 at 4:08PM EST

Although Nvidia (NVDA -2.90%) just delivered another incredible earnings report, investors are preoccupied with the unexpected departure of founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang. During the company's earnings call, board chairman Harvey Jones made it clear that Nvidia intends to move forward without its former leader. Jones said the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him.

However, Huang may have another way to influence Nvidia's future. According to a recent Reuters report, Nvidia's corporate governance rules grant the former CEO the ability to nominate two candidates for election to the company's board of directors.

At this time, there is no public evidence that Huang intends to exercise that right. Nevertheless, I think Tesla (TSLA +0.95%) CEO Elon Musk and CrowdStrike (CRWD +7.95%) CEO George Kurtz make two compelling hypothetical candidates. Here's why.

Nvidia's definitive proxy statement from May 12, 2026 outlines a shareholder nomination mechanism known as proxy access. Under the company's bylaws, shareholders who have controlled at least 3% of Nvidia's voting power for three consecutive years can nominate candidates for inclusion in its annual proxy materials. The number of candidates is limited to the greater of two directors or 20% of the board.

Huang has maintained ownership above that threshold for more than three years and currently controls approximately 3.5% of Nvidia. Importantly, this authority comes from Huang's position as a qualifying shareholder rather than a special privilege granted with founding Nvidia.

The proxy statement specifies that nominations for Nvidia's 2027 annual shareholder meeting must be submitted between Feb. 24 and March 26, 2027. It is important to note that nominating directors does not guarantee their election. Shareholders still need to vote on the candidates, and nominees must meet Nvidia's independence standards and other governance requirements.

Nevertheless, board composition matters greatly because directors oversee corporate strategy and executive succession planning. If Huang nominates candidates who share his vision for Nvidia's future, they could potentially influence other directors over time.

Elon Musk is easily one of the most provocative hypothetical nominees. Musk's companies are major buyers and suppliers within the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem. Moreover, his ambitions extend beyond purchasing Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs). Musk's proposed Terafab semiconductor manufacturing initiative underscores his interest in developing new types of compute capacity to support future AI development.

Sitting on Nvidia's board could theoretically give Musk an opportunity to help shape the direction of one of the world's leading AI infrastructure companies. His experience building Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies also brings an unconventional perspective on manufacturing, capital investment, and innovation roadmaps.

However, commercial relationships between Musk's businesses and Nvidia, as well as potential competition with Terafab, would require scrutiny under the company's independence and conflict-of-interest rules.

George Kurtz is a different but equally interesting possibility. His professional relationship with Huang is supported by a strategic partnership between CrowdStrike and Nvidia. In September, Huang joined Kurtz at CrowdStrike's Fal.Con conference to introduce SafeMind, an agentic cybersecurity system incorporating Nvidia's Nemotron technology.

Huang has previously emphasized that cybersecurity will become one of AI's most compute-intensive applications, positioning CrowdStrike as an important partner in Nvidia's expansion beyond AI model training.

Of course, Kurtz's relationship with Nvidia also creates potential conflicts that would need to be evaluated before any nomination. Still, his experience in enterprise software and established working relationship with Huang make him an interesting candidate for a board seat.

Corporate boards are rarely unanimous on every single decision. For this reason, newly elected directors could potentially encourage the board to reconsider a decision that initially appeared final.

However, there are some obstacles to this scenario. Board members have fiduciary obligations to Nvidia and its shareholders. This means they must evaluate strategy and leadership decisions independently rather than simply following the wishes of the shareholder who nominated them.

Timing presents the biggest challenge, because Nvidia could appoint a new CEO well before its 2027 annual meeting. This means that even if Huang nominated two successful candidates, reversing the company's leadership transition would require support from additional directors.

Regardless, Huang's proxy-access provision introduces a governance consideration that investors shouldn't overlook. His substantial ownership still gives him an indirect avenue to influence Nvidia's future, even after resigning. Whether he chooses to exercise that right is not yet known, but even the possibility could keep speculation surrounding his return alive.

For investors, the big-picture issue is whether Nvidia can preserve its innovation, strategic relationships, and competitive advantages established under Huang's tenure. Ultimately, Nvidia's ability to execute its AI strategy under new leadership is more important than the possibility of a dramatic boardroom comeback.
