#3044. Disney Imagineers Have Built AI-Powered ‘Star Wars’ Alien Audio-Animatronics With AWS

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Semi-exclusive: Three original Anzellan characters with distinct personalities will interact with guests in Disney parks.

Disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland. But today, new robotic characters are being powered up with artificial intelligence.

In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three new Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

Anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe. They include Babu Frik in Star Wars: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker and the droidsmiths introduced in season 3 of The Mandalorian. The droidsmiths take on larger roles in The Mandalorian and Grogu, helping Baby Yoda rescue Din Djarin from the Hutts.

The new Anzellan animatronics built by Disney Imagineers use AWS cloud and AI capabilities in order to “understand the scene around them,” Kyle Laughlin, SVP of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, tells me.

“If you imagine walking into an experiential retail store, you now will be greeted not by a pre-scripted animation or interaction, but a totally personalized experience where each of these Anzellans [has] their own personalities,” Laughlin says, adding that they’ll be attuned to how many people are nearby and whether they’re children or adults.

The animatronic aliens will be able to interact with guests, right down to commenting on people who are wearing a birthday button or even a certain Star Wars T-shirt. Speaking with these animatronics will give guests the same experience they would have when meeting a character walking around the park, Laughlin adds. They also play off each other and react to what each other are doing, with no one controlling them behind the scenes.

The three audio-animatronic prototypes, which will make their first appearance during AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas on Nov. 30 before moving into one of the Disney Parks, are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a.

They’re original characters created just for this project in partnership with Lucasfilm and the filmmakers, and they all have their own personalities devised by the Imagineers. Vilo is the boss, Kado is the droidsmith mechanic who wants to be the center of attention and Jibu, though Kado’s twin, is the shy one. The animatronics speak a mix of English (or Galactic Basic in-universe) and Anzellan, as they do in the Star Wars movies and TV series, and have hundreds of thousands of prerecorded lines of dialogue to draw from when talking to guests and each other.

Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising and Sports, tells me this is “one of the most delightful examples” of physical AI.

“When you talk about physical AI, it’s AI that perceives, it reasons and it acts in the real world,” she says. “It’s not just AI on a screen.”

Bakhtiar says Disney was able to use both AWS cloud computing and AI tools to “get from idea to implementation several magnitudes faster than they would have otherwise,” with Laughlin specifying it took “mere months.”

AWS staff used a coding agent called Kiro that built their creative briefs into software, which was then reviewed and approved by humans. Imagineers also used the Amazon Bedrock fully managed AI service, which allows them to choose between all the biggest AI models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

“We’re providing Amazon Bedrock to the Imagineering team to be able to leverage the right models that they need at the right time to be able to really enhance those character experiences,” Bakhtiar tells me. “From multimodal models that focus on voice to world models, to large language models. The point is that they are able to get the right tool at the right time and then do so in a way that’s secure, resilient, performant and globally available.”

Bakhtiar says AWS is continuing to work with Disney, though the next project is under wraps.

“The future of entertainment is going to be highly personalized,” she says. “It’s going to be multidimensional, and it’s going to be more interactive than ever. And I think this is an incredible example of that coming to life.”

Disney had previously teamed up with Nvidia on robotics and AI to bring a robot version of fan-favorite Frozen character Olaf to life so he can wander around Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland, and is also now exploring robots paired with AI that could guide guests throughout Disneyland parking lots.

“You can imagine an entire franchise of characters working and interacting with one another,” says Laughlin. “We’ve done a number of things in the Star Wars universe. We’re just getting started in Frozen, and we have a wealth of IP that we can mine to bring those characters to our guests as fast as possible.”

Correction, 3:48 p.m. ET: The original version of this story incorrectly stated who used the Kiro coding agent to build the software. It was staff from AWS.

#3043. Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The company also released new ROI tracking tools for companies monitoring their AI spend.

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

Asset sales and mining margin pressure shape the quarter's deleveraging push.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 18, 2026 at 4:23PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Siderúrgica Nacional (SID -5.89%) reported a decrease in quarterly earnings as margin compression in the mining segment and unfavorable freight conditions offset gains in its other divisions. Management indicated that the company is executing a deleveraging plan through the divestment of noncore assets, including the sale of its cement subsidiary and a German steel unit. The company intends to rebalance its capital structure by extending debt maturities and reducing inventory levels while focusing capital expenditures on the P15 iron ore expansion project. These events may differ materially from those expressed herein, and therefore, they do not constitute projections. In fact, actual results, performance, or events may differ materially from those expressed or implied by forward-looking statements as a result of several factors such as general and economic conditions in Brazil and other countries, interest rates and exchange rate levels, future rescheduling or prepayment of debt denominated in foreign currencies, protectionist measures in the U.S., Brazil, and other countries, changes in law and regulations, and general competitive factors both globally, regionally, or nationally.

I would now like to turn over the floor to Mr. Fabio Schvartsman, the company's CEO, who will present the financial and operating highlights of CSN. You may proceed, Mr. Schvartsman.

Fabio Schvartsman: A good day to all of you. This is the first opportunity that I have of coming into contact with the investors. As you well know, I have been at CSN for a little more than two months, and since I took on this position, I wanted to conclude the negotiations that were underway for the assets that are under sale and learn about the company. In this call specifically, I would like to proceed in the following way. I will turn the floor over to Pedro Oliva, who will present the results. After this, we will go on to the question-and-answer session.

Of course, your questions will be of prime importance to allow me to understand what it is that you would like me to share with you, which is what I will do. For the time being, Pedro Oliva will present the results, and we will then go on to the Q&A session.

Pedro Oliva: Good morning, everybody. I will begin the presentation with the highlights for the third quarter 2026. Adjusted EBITDA reached BRL 1.87 billion, down 32% and 43% year-on-year, with a margin of 17%. This performance reflects the more challenging price and freight conditions in mining and the negative seasonality in the foreign market for steel sales and vacation period in Europe. Higher raw material costs in cement and steel production leverage reached 4.23x pressured by a combination of lower EBITDA, higher volume of debt amortizations, and iron ore prepayment contract. However, the signing of the SWT term sheet and the sale of CSN Cimentos reinforce the efforts being made to improve the capital structure.

Instead of going through all of this information, I will simply refer to the figures on the following slide. Adjusted EBITDA totaled BRL 1.876 billion, and this drop is reflected because of the margin compression in mining. Now, you can see the drop in the price of iron ore and an increase in maritime freight, accounting for the weakness in the period. We had an extraordinary Jacuí effect in energy the previous quarter also contributing to this decline. In the following slide, we have data on investment. CapEx of BRL 1.38 billion with a reduction of 2% in the quarter, with a greater optimization of maintenance investments offsetting the full acceleration in CapEx for the P15.

Regarding working capital, net working capital totaled BRL 2.2 billion, down 27.7% quarter-on-quarter. The reduction mainly reflects a strategy of lowering inventory to optimize operations and release working capital. The lower accounts receivable balance in line with a reduced commercial activity also contributed to the result. Now, the free cash flow was negative at BRL 3.5 billion in the third quarter, reversing the positive result of the previous quarter. Weaker operating performance and a concentration of debt amortizations and iron ore prepayment more than offset the release of working capital and the initiatives being implemented to reduce cash burn. Consolidated net debt reached BRL 44.9 billion in the third quarter, and leverage rose to 4.23x.

Lower last 12 months EBITDA, especially due to the margin compression in mining and the concentration of amortization, have pressured the indicator. In this regard, progress on asset sale projects, the binding term sheet for the full divestment of the subsidiary SWT, and the sale agreement of CSN Cimentos to Huaxin are solid evidence of all the efforts being made to improve the group's capital structure. When it comes to the indebtedness profile, CSN continues to act towards lengthening the maturities and adjust its capital structure. In the third quarter 2026, the main development was a successful note exchange offer aimed to extend by two years the maturity of BRL 1.3 billion originally due in 2028.

This transaction had more than 77% acceptance and allowed the company to significantly extend its expected amortization profile for the coming years. In the next slide, we can highlight the advance of the asset sale process. On November 8, CSN announced the signing of the agreement of the sale of CSN Cimentos. This shows the company's commitment to financial discipline and a focus on deleveraging.

I am a witness that this was a core issue for investors throughout the year since the company in January announced its plan of deleveraging between 16 billion and 18 billion, and the progress of all of this shows that the company is executing what it has set forth to do and is ready to do whatever it has to reach the deleveraging it desires. Regarding CSN Cimentos, the enterprise value was BRL 12.7 billion, with an equity value of BRL 9 billion, 8.1x EV/EBITDA, higher than other companies in the same sector. Now, this represents 100% of stake. It was mentioned that it would be up to 100%.

The company decided to carry out an integral sale to reduce the leverage. The operation, of course, is subject to regulatory approvals that are underway and advancing. There is a possibility that the closing will happen still during this year. If this does not happen, there is an initiative to anticipate a relevant part of the equity value in 2026 to take advantage of these fiscal losses anticipated. The closing could also happen in 2027, and this context will become ever more important. In the transaction of SWT, the transaction value is EUR 550 million, EV/EBITDA 11.2x. Due diligence and negotiation documents are ongoing. Expected closing, December of 2026.

We are awaiting the regulatory approval with the antitrust agency in Germany. This has already begun, and the documents have been submitted. The impact of these two transactions represents BRL 16.1 billion, which shows you that the company has delivered what it set forth to do at the beginning of the year. Let's go on to the highlights of the year with steel. In the domestic market, we had stable sales in the quarter, but up 5.8% year-on-year, despite the resurgence of imports, especially in September. In the foreign market, down 14.7% in the quarter due to seasonality, but up 10% year-on-year as a result of better steel consumption in the European market.

In the following slide, the slab production reached 776,000 tons in the third quarter, the best result for the year, reflecting the greater efficiency of the productions process across UPV. Plate costs remained stable at BRL 3,394 per ton, even in a quarter with raw material cost pressures. On the following slide, we see the financial performance where the steel mill net revenue reached BRL 5.75 billion, a drop of 5.3% in the quarter, reflecting seasonality and foreign operations. On a year-on-year basis, revenue rose 8.6%. Adjusted EBITDA was BRL 576.1 million, with a 10% margin, very similar to that of the previous quarter.

Going on to mining, we had production of iron ore, including third-party purchases of 9.9 million tons, a 9% decline due to higher rainfall volumes and a temporary reduction in the lower-quality dry ore because of the market conditions. Sales, on the other hand, were practically stable despite lower production in the period, showing that the company has advanced in its inventory reduction efforts to sustain the volume. TECAR shipped 10.373 million tons in the period, up 6.4%, reinforcing the efficiency of its logistics structure. In financial performance of mining, net revenue was BRL 2.308 billion, a drop of 18% quarter-on-quarter.

Lower iron ore prices and their impact on provisional price, along with higher freight costs, reduced unit revenue to $40, a reduction of $9 vis-à-vis the previous quarter. Adjusted EBITDA, in turn, was BRL 380 million, with a 16% margin in the third quarter. In adjusted EBITDA, reconciliation of EBITDA, we see which are the offenders, and the price per se explained BRL 417 million of drop in EBITDA in mining. Going on to cement, sales volume reached 3.444 million tons in the quarter, the highest volume of the year, up 10% vis-à-vis the previous quarter. The effective commercial policy of CSN sustained performance even in a period marked by heavy rainfall and fewer business days.

Regarding the financial performance, net revenue reached BRL 1.45 billion, up 4.7% in the quarter and 8.8% year-on-year, as a result of intense commercial activity and price readjustments implemented throughout the year. Adjusted EBITDA was BRL 385 million, a 9.7% decline, with a 26% margin. Higher raw material costs and freight costs pressured the profitability in the period. This is the impact of pet coke that increased 99% compared with the first quarter of this year. Regarding logistics, we go to the financial performance. Net revenue of 1.2 billion was practically in line with recent quarters, with the rail and port segments offsetting the weaker performance of multimodal logistics.

Adjusted EBITDA was BRL 533 million, a slight decline of 2%, with a 44% margin. I would like to highlight the resilience of performance in logistics. Despite a more adverse scenario of iron ore, they continue to deliver margins above 40% and EBITDA higher than BRL 500 million. Going on to energy, we had net revenue of BRL 176 million in the third quarter, a 55% decline, reflecting the normalization of results after the extraordinary Jacuí effect in the second quarter. Adjusted EBITDA, in turn, reached BRL 45 million, with a margin of 25%. With this, we conclude the presentation. We can now go on to the question-and-answer session.

Operator: Well, thank you. We will now go on to the question-and-answer session for investors and market analysts. Should you have a question, please click on the raise hand icon or send your question through the Q&A icon. Our first question comes from Rodolfo De Angele from JPMorgan. Your microphone has been unmuted, sir. You may proceed.

Rodolfo De Angele: Good morning, and thank you. Fabio, congratulations for your entry into the company. I have a single question for you, Fabio. I would like for you to discuss with us which was the motivation for you to join and by your say, short term, and how all of this will play out. Thank you.

Fabio Schvartsman: Well, thank you for your question, Rodolfo. It's a good beginning, explaining why I have come to the company. Well, first of all, we need to respect and praise the fact that my predecessor and main shareholder in the company, Benjamin, decided to pass all of this on to me. He thought it was a moment to carry out this change because this allows the company to do what it has to do with speed and precision. Personally, there's a very interesting issue, which is the following.

There is a certain parallelism with my passage through Klabin that you followed up on, and nobody outside of the company or the family had ever managed Klabin until I took on that position. Klabin was also undergoing a very difficult moment. I looked at that, and during the period in which I remained there, and after the first six months, I was able to see an improvement in results, and they continued to improve quarter on quarter until I left. After I left the company, the results continued to improve continuously, showing that this is not ephemeral work. It was something that had transformed the company in the way that it should be changed.

I would be very satisfied if I am able to do something similar in CSN. There needs to be a change in that direction. It's too early on to say what will be done and which will be the sequence of changes. I remind you that in the last two months, my focus has been on doing what had to be done to settle the sale of assets operation that would allow for an initial rebalancing of the company's structure. Based on that, we could begin our work for a review of how the company operates.

I also draw your attention to what was mentioned in the results release, both for mining and here, that we have a short-term problem in mining. It's the extremely low price of iron ore and the high and steep price of freight. We have no control whatsoever of what happens with prices. In the case of CSN, that has mines of excellent quality, CSN is working on the P15 project that should be completed and be in full operation in 2029. That is to say, in two years, where we will fully see the results of our investment, and this will change the dependence of CSN on the mining and freight cycles.

We're speaking of a short horizon that needs to be overcome so that we can begin working in a completely different way regarding the other businesses of the group. As you have observed, they're relatively stable. We have no immediate problems that require a solution. Now, to continue with this long-winded answer, I always thought that managing was doing the obvious things right, and there's nothing different here. This is what we will do here. We will do whatever we need to do to ensure that the company can gain a rebalance and present the potential results it could present.

Finally, part of my learning in the company is to get to know and acknowledge the quality of the assets that CSN has, allows us to have strong expectations going forward, and after the work that we need to carry out, the company will reach another level. Almost certainly, we'll reach another level. Thank you.

Rodolfo De Angele: Thank you very much, and the best of luck.

Operator: Our next question comes from Daniel Sasson from Itaú BBA. Your microphone has been unmuted. You may proceed.

Daniel Sasson: Good morning, everybody. A good day. Thank you for taking my questions. Welcome, Fabio, and good luck with this challenge. My first question refers to the guidance for the final leverage of the year of 3x compared to 4.3x in the third quarter. The closing or the sale of cement is expected only for 2027. So, this 3x guidance for the end of the year, is this still standing? How will you reduce the 4.3x to only 3x leverage? There must be pressure on the last 12 months EBITDA in the last quarter. So, are you going to review that guidance considering the novel conditions?

Still referring to the restructuring of assets, Fabio, you spoke about the quality of the assets at CSN. You were able to conclude the sale of cement as SWT expected by the market. If you could comment on the result of a minority sale of the infrastructure business. How are you going to structure this, the contracts between TECAR and CSN Mining, so that the entry of a third party will not transfer all of the cost to CSN, impacting the EBITDA? These are my questions. Thank you.

Fabio Schvartsman: Thank you very much, Daniel. First of all, at this point in time, it is still not possible to state if an operation will be necessary in that case because of the indebtedness guidance. We are assessing the impacts of the sale of the cement plant, and in truth, additionally, we are structuring things in such a way that we can anticipate the reception as part of this exercise. This process is ongoing. It has not been concluded. I cannot state if that will happen, in fact. Consequently, we have to wait for the conclusion of this work to have a better idea of which will be the guidance that the company will offer in terms of leverage.

Once this work is carried out, we will inform the market. Your question refers to the infrastructure assets. What I was able to observe so far is that the idea of selling a minority stake in infrastructure is not the best way to monetize the company's assets. If we continue along those lines, we will sell the assets off individually. Of course, we are not speaking of all assets. Some are more strategic than others, so each one will be a case apart. Notwithstanding this, more importantly than this is to state that we are progressing at present in the sale of other assets.

As you can imagine, given the fact that these are negotiations underway, I cannot explain to you which they are. I don't have that liberty. Our expectation is to have responses in the short term regarding these additional negotiations. Obviously, all of this will be part of the guidance that we will set forth in the future.

Daniel Sasson: Thank you, Fabio. That was very clear.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mr. Leo Correa from BTG Pactual. Your audio has been unmuted. You may proceed.

Leo Correa: Is everything okay? Good afternoon to all of you. Fabio, I would also like to begin that I have been following on your career for many years, and to hear you once again and speak to you once again allows me to wish you much luck in this new stage. The topic is somewhat difficult, so I will focus my questions on leverage. It's very clear, Fabio, that the short-term scenario is highly challenging because of what happens with iron ore. This may be cyclical. The fact is that the company is burning BRL 2 billion-BRL 3 billion in cash per quarter, which means that part of the sale of assets will be put at risk.

That target of BRL 18 billion in the sale of assets was based on a scenario of a different EBITDA vis-à-vis the present-day scenario. My question, therefore, in those short two months in which you have come and looking at the scenario, which is a change in your deleveraging and asset sale goal, can you share anything with us? This would be very helpful for us. A natural question that arises is that if, Casa de Pedra mine has always been the jewel of the crown, it was being put aside in this investment plan that was focusing on cement.

I would like to hear about you, about this new environment, and if that will come back to the table for a new negotiation. We know that Itochu is one of your partners, or perhaps others could get involved in this sale. A second question, Fabio. The CSN amortization schedule was shared with us, and it is very evident that the large company disbursements are with local banks. Approximately BRL 1.5 billion still this year, and almost BRL 6 billion in banking debts maturing the coming year in 2027. As far as I understand this debt has no warranties so far. How are your negotiations proceeding with local banks in terms of rolling this debt? These are my two questions.

Fabio Schvartsman: Well, thank you for your comments and for the questions. Let us begin with the second question, the rolling of a debt, and I would like to go back to a comment I made at the beginning. When I entered the company, I focused on selling off the assets that were under sale for the good of the company, and this has been done. Obviously, that meant I was devoted to negotiations with bank about rolling the debt or similar issues. It is evident, nevertheless, that we are now talking about negotiating with the banks to roll the debts, an extension of term, and a reduction in the interest rate for the company.

This has to be the focus, and this is what we will do going forward. Managing is to do the obvious things, and for things to work, we focus on one thing per time. If we try to do everything together, we end up doing nothing. The next focus is exactly this one. Personally, I will devote myself to that, and we will do whatever is necessary to allow this to proceed. What we will receive for the sale of assets and if cement is part of this process or not, as I mentioned, at this stage, I cannot mention which are the negotiations underway. I can state once again that we will do whatever is necessary.

This includes the sale of assets to reach a stable level in the financial structure of the company. It is obvious that we have no other alternative.

Leo Correa: That is very clear. Thank you, Fabio.

Operator: Our next question comes from Ricardo Monegaglia from Safra. Your microphone has been unmuted.

Ricardo Monegaglia: Good morning to everybody. Thank you for taking our question, and congratulations for the announcement of the sale of cement. I think this is very important to have a healthier leverage. I am going to focus less here on the objective parts of leveraging. I would like to hear from you how you are going to add your expertise in mining to the assets at cement and the steel plant. We are undergoing difficult moments in both segments, but the doubt perhaps that is pending is, and as you mentioned, with iron ore and freight, we have no control over that.

What is it that we can expect from the operations that changes to have a healthier level of results without thinking about commodities, CapEx efficiency, others that are not part of your focus? We could have an interesting discussion once the company ends up in a healthier position in terms of leverage. I don't know if this is a coincidence or not. We have noticed that the buybacks had a very short time, and then they ceased. How do you consider the buyback strategy at cement at present? Is this something that we might see if the scenario of freighting is better, or are you not intending to structure this going forward?

If you're truly going to focus on deleveraging everywhere that is possible, and the rolling of the debt, and to focus on lower-cost debts, the same point and the same question, are you already interacting with the bank owners? We have a market that, well, you could access once again if the global credit situation improves. Is there anything that you can share about these initial contacts with bondholders, especially the foreigners?

Fabio Schvartsman: Well, thank you for your question, Ricardo. Once again, beginning with the last one, I hadn't even spoken to the investors yet, and of course, I haven't spoken to the bondholders up to present. We have to do first things first, of course. First of all, we're focusing on the financial structure of the company, and eventually, I will be able to converse with bondholders and speak about the topic you mentioned. There's no problem regarding that. Now, the buyback, it relates directly to the price of share and company results. Company results at this point do not recommend holding a buyback.

If the results recover and if the price of shares do not recover, the buyback opportunity will still be there, and we will make the most of it, especially because we're selling off assets, which means we're receiving cash that allows us to do positive things for the company based on that cash. I'm sorry, which was your first question?

Ricardo Monegaglia: Which are the opportunities that you see to bring in your expertise in mining and business for the other assets where the results are under pressure, and perhaps to only depend on the commodities will not bring about the enhancement that you expect?

Fabio Schvartsman: Once again, I'm going to say something that is very obvious, and I apologize for this. The price of a commodity and freight, this is what controls the results of any company, whether it is Vale, CSN, or any other mining company. As a consequence, CapEx efficiency or OpEx management, of course, they're all very helpful, but they have a marginal effect in the results we need to obtain. To speak very frankly and clearly, which is how I normally proceed in these issues, CSN has a beautiful project, the P15, that will be ready in a very short time. It will radically change the condition of the company when it comes to producing results.

This is the focus, to ensure P15 will come in and as soon as possible. By doing that, we will have very good news to disclose. The rest are minor things that will not significantly alter anything. Price, iron ore, and freight, they are either cyclical or impacted by the geopolitical scenario. Yes, they will have changes going forward. Nobody has a crystal ball to say when this will happen, but that's the nature of the business. I have already seen this in mining and pulp and paper. That's how those scenarios operate. There's not very much that you can do.

You have to be steadfast, do what has to be done during that period, which is what we will do here. Thank you.

Ricardo Monegaglia: Thank you very much. Success, Fabio. I wish you success.

Operator: Our next question comes from Henrique Marques from Goldman Sachs. You may proceed, sir. Your microphone has been unmuted.

Henrique Marques: Good morning, everybody. Thank you for taking my question. A follow-up in terms of the company's financial structure that has been discussed at length here. We see the company following the steps of the strategic plan set forth at the beginning of the year. How far will this financial restructuring go? Which is the target that you would like to reach to get to that point where you say, "We have done what had to be done"? Is there a gross profit target, a leverage target? Another question, moving away a bit from the plan and speaking about the market situation, especially in steel. We see that the demand continues to be resilient.

Imports are better behaved than one year ago. Whatever has now been approved seems to have worked. Now, changes at those levels, will they help? The outlook of most of the steel mills is a flat outlook. Which is the great detractor of that industry? Is it the inventories that are too high, readjustment, indirect imports? And which is the solution for all of this? Because eventually, anti-dumping measures for direct imports are very tiresome, and they take forever. For steel companies, how can they go back to the levels of profitability that they had last year, for example, and the expectation for 2027?

Fabio Schvartsman: Now, things will work in a process when it comes to our main goal. Our main goal is to deliver P15 up and running in mid-2028 so that it could come into full operation in 2029. Now, to define what the deleveraging level is, gross debt, and much more, all relates to whatever is necessary to attain our goal, and this is how we will proceed. I have no figures to give you regarding this situation. We're working on this, and that is our priority at present, as I mentioned. Regarding the steel mill, I will give the floor to whoever understands this, Mr. Martinez, who will speak about his vision going forward for steel.

Steel, anticipating what Martinez will say, has more upsides than downsides at present. Martinez, please.

Luis Martinez: Thank you, Fabio. Henrique, allow me five minutes to give you an overview of what is happening worldwide and how we address this issue of profitability. It's not only for steel mills in Brazil. We're going to see what is happening globally. First of all, and these are facts that I'm going to repeat, U.S. has had full success of the anti-dumping measures, the 232. Demand is strong. The machines are working full steam. We look at the results of American plants, and we can't ignore what is happening there.

There's a Nucor in the third quarter with 20%, SDI with 18%, and this is the best mirror that we can have to observe the market in Brazil to try to find something similar. Now, to give you an idea, if we don't redress the situation in Brazil, if we don't do what needs to be done, we have room for some exports to the U.S.A. vis-à-vis the present-day prices in the American market. This is a situation of the U.S.A. In Europe, the most important thing done presently was to reduce 50% the quotas for other countries, and the immediate impact is that prices increased EUR 120, EUR 130 during the period. Now, some of these solutions are hateful.

In Europe, they're working with a margin of 8%, others with a margin of 6%. So, these are the portraits of situations that are completely different, and we see Europe going towards the situation we have in the U.S.A. Finally, when we go to China, and China has important things to mention, the real estate market, this is no novelty, represents 30% of the GDP. It has had a huge fall. The price of the cement ton that was $50 is now around $25-$30. On the other hand, China decided to grow expressively in manufactured products. The largest exports of China are in indirect and finished products, obviously going into all of the value chains throughout the world.

To give you an idea, in Korea, profitability of a Hyundai is 7% and Nippon Steel 11% or 9%. These are margins of countries that brilliantly are resisting the invasion by the Chinese. When we look at prices worldwide, we see China with BQ prices of $480, $500, U.S.A. with a price of $1,500, and Europe with the increases I just mentioned of $850. In this scenario, there's no way not to impact what will happen in Brazil. I tend to convey optimistic views. We're getting to the point where we're going to have to turn the key.

Despite the retraction and apparent consumption in the country of 2%-3%, domestic sales have increased 3%, and CSN this year will grow 8%-10% in terms of volume. When we look at the sectors, in truth, we're looking at the automotive sector. There is strong imports. Manufactured products are doing well, white line, 3%-5%. Now, where the market is more difficult, it's in agriculture implements and machinery suffering somewhat more because of the interest rates and funding, and you can fully understand what is happening there in imports that you mentioned as well. This is interesting data. Look at the paradox we have reached here. The largest steel importers from China have become the greatest exporters of steel to Brazil.

This shows you how fragile Brazil is in terms of its commercial policy and valuing its own industry. We have two countries, Vietnam and Korea, who are practically occupying the position of China in some products. Another important fact, despite the imports of steel dropping 18%-20% per year, 4 million approximately, it grew 20% are the exports of China in terms of manufactured products. This is more than 5 million of steel here, and there are examples that are also interesting, 185% growth in cars, and two that I captured here to show you how aggressive that purpose is of a country like China, along with other Asian nations.

We are receiving in Brazil 79% more packaging, empty cans, and 40% of gas bottles, also empty. This clearly shows you how unprepared we are for changes of policy in terms of what is happening worldwide. When we speak about the risk of imports nowadays, because of the anti-dumping activities against the Chinese, it is no longer worthwhile bringing products from China. We are awaiting the decision of the government that should take place at the end of this month or in December, the implementation of anti-dumping of hot-rolled plates. Nowadays, the risk of imports is a reasonable risk, 10%-15%, that we can work with here because of the risk of service, risk of exchange rate.

From the viewpoint of a commercial defense, the point you mentioned is important. We have a very strong schedule of commercial defense. As I said, we implemented all of the anti-dumping policies. We are working for the one of BQ, and in the case of CSN, at the end of November and December, anti-dumping for tinplate from Germany, the Netherlands, and Japan. This should also help us positively. Regarding the commercial defense, geopolitical defense, and what happens worldwide, Brazil needs to have the project of a nation, Mexico, for example, looking at the upstream industries and trying to create a competitive isonomy between them. The last point I would like to mention is cost.

To give you an idea, the cost of raw material has a direct impact. For example, coal and pet coke with increases of $190 to $250, it is inevitable not to have a price correction in the market. We have covered cost. There is the issue of the dollar. We considered it at BRL 4.95. It is presently BRL 5.65. The value chains and imports. Based on that scenario, what do we believe? I believe that this is going to happen whether we like it or not. There is a mandatory correction of prices of 14%-16% on November 9th.

We had an increase in the distribution channels, civil construction, the assembly industry, an increase of 7.5% for December, another increase between 5%-7.5% to redress this ridiculous difference in terms of raw material. For assembly lines of the white line, automobiles for the beginning of the year, when we renew contracts, we will begin negotiations with a 10% of correction. This will include exchange rate and raw material. The demand scenario is not fully favorable, but it is possible because domestic sales are growing. This is a price correction governed by cost, and this is what rules in the market at present. I hope to have given you a vision of what is happening here in Brazil.

Henrique Marques: That was excellent. Very clear. Thank you.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mr. Arthur from UBS. Your microphone has been unmuted. You may proceed.

Mr: Thank you for taking my question. I have a question that is more strategic regarding cement. CSN now is losing an asset with high margins, with a more predictable cash generation, and when we look at mining, which is the main asset of the group, they become ever more exposed to iron ore and freight. How are you going to reduce the volatility of cash generation going forward after the sale of CSN Cimentos without further increasing the impact on mining? My second question, in the steel mill, you need capital for streamlining, as was mentioned. You have margins pressured by imports, low utilization, and costs.

Which is the minimum return that the management should demand from the segment, and if this return cannot be reached organically, if the company will reduce the exposure of the steel mills, look for a strategic partner, and perhaps separate the business. Thank you.

Fabio Schvartsman: Wow, that is a question and some. How to reduce the volatility of a cyclical business. There are some normal instruments that can be used, closing the freight beforehand, work with iron ore protection. This can produce savings if this is done correctly. Now, from the viewpoint of mining, what will change substantially the exposure, as I mentioned, is the P15. We have the expectation of an additional of $40 per ton in whatever is sold as iron ore going through P15. This is substantial and will significantly alter the volatility of the company, but that is in two years. Therefore, before those two years, there's no way to significantly change the volatility.

Regarding the steel mill, it may need investments, large investments in the long term, but it is presently in a stable condition. It can produce good results as is with minor investments, which is what we will continue to do. Now, regarding strategic changes in the company, I confirm, as you already know, but I can state that this is also my opinion after joining the company, that we have very good assets that will be used to benefit the deleveraging of the company. I cannot and don't want to go in further details at this point, but in a relatively short term, you will see these changes. A substantial change in the company strategy cannot be achieved overnight.

It would not be realistic to think that we're going to do a 180% shift in the company immediately. We are going to build something solid through time, as I was able to do in the former companies where I worked. Here, the situation will not be different. We have very good assets at the start, and the prices may be very low because of the present-day situation, but these situations come and go. Consequently, the price of assets will appear, and this will be reflected positively in the company.

The only good news in all of this is that we're at the bottom of the well, and there's only one path possible for the moment, which is upwards and out of this.

Operator: Thank you. Our next question comes from [Paula Athanassakis] from Citi. Your audio has been unmuted.

Speaker 10: Thank you. Thank you for taking our questions. I'd like to ask a question about the fourth quarter. In the third quarter, you released your working capital, and you mentioned that you had carried out significant efforts towards decreasing the inventory. Now, for the fourth quarter, can we also expect another release of working capital because of the inventory, or has the main effort already been done in this quarter? A question about steel. You commented on the increases you will have in November, and once again, further price increases in December. Which has been the feedback of the customers so far?

If we consider that the situation is not simple, and the cost pressure, could you give us an idea of which is the increase you would have in steel? Thank you. Thank you very much.

Fabio Schvartsman: Thank you for the question, Paula. I will answer the first and then give the floor to Martinez regarding working capital. You are right. The best result has already been achieved since January up to present. We reduced BRL 1.9 billion from January to September, but we still foresee some opportunities going forward, especially in the steel mill. There are some elements that we can work with to further reduce inventory, and we are quantifying that opportunity to add BRL 900 million until the end of the year. Martinez?

Luis Martinez: Paula, I am going to repeat what I said in the last question, basically. To look at the efficacy of a price increase, it will be easier or more difficult according to the value chain. We have a price correction that needs to be carried out because of the cost, because of the exchange rate. It is BRL 5.65 at present compared to BRL 4.95, a huge gap. Now the premium for the nationalized imports, perhaps they are weakened in terms of the long steel. The result is almost negative there. On the 9th, we implemented an increase. There was no negotiation here. There is not very much we can do with this first increase.

I consider the increase implemented on November 9. We still have included chains that have a semestral contract. For December, we do have that challenge of conversing with the value chain, speaking about what is happening in terms of cost, and for you to maintain the profitability that we have set forth. It is also mandatory to correct prices when it comes to cost. Although we have KPIs under control, we have an enormous project for operational excellence at the plant to reduce cost, to work with a lower cost for coke, to work with less residues, to get to a cost, despite the increase in raw material.

This increase is mandatory to reach those margins of 15%, which is what I set forth as a target going forward.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mr. Guilherme Nippes from XP. You can proceed with your question, sir.

Guilherme Nippes: Good afternoon. Thank you for taking my questions. Fabio, a great deal of success in this new challenge. My first question, going back to cash generation. I am sorry to insist on this. What we have observed here is that increase of pace in cash burn in the last quarters because of the operational situation under pressure. I would like to know if there is another alternative to reduce that cash burn in the short term, if there is a limit to the reduction of this cash burn, and other alternatives to release cash. In the past, you had mentioned monetization of assets, a sale of real estate, working capital, as you mentioned now, more space for working capital.

If there are other alternatives we can think about to improve the cash context that is under pressure. This would help us a great deal. My second question, a follow-up of the previous question, with the cost of the steel mill, to see if everything is clear, your expectation for the fourth quarter. The expectation is relatively flat costs. Is that it, or is there something different? Thank you.

Fabio Schvartsman: Allow me to speak about the short-term things we are doing, controlling and reducing CapEx to the necessary minimum in all of the companies. These are factors that produce cash. They have been producing cash constantly, and we cannot change the logic that the results are being pressured because of the situation of the commodities. As I mentioned before, we have very good assets, and we are going to use these assets to help us improve the company's situation in this period of greater turbulence. Besides that, there are no novelties. Obviously, everything that we can do in terms of cost-cutting has been done as we speak. All of these traditional measures are all underway.

Luis Martinez: Guilherme, to speak a bit more about the steel mill, I reiterate what has already been done in the last few years. Enormous efforts towards operational excellence, and we have worked successfully our expectation for the cost of plates. Despite the increase in raw material, we work with a stable cost for slabs, plates. When it comes to inventories that we mentioned, this year we have reduced BRL 1 billion in finished products until the end of the year. Regarding cash, the idea is to work with a minimum stock of finished products and intermediate products. The goal for cash, it is something we will continue to pursue. From the viewpoint of EBITDA, there is no simple equation.

The price has to increase and the cost has to remain the same to have an EBITDA margin that is higher than 10% or 15%. I truly believe that every time we have a significant cost issue, the steel mill manages to come out somewhat better in terms of a price realignment in the market. Thank you for the question.

Guilherme Nippes: Well, thank you. Thank you.

Operator: We would like to remind you that should you wish to pose a question, please click on the raise hand icon or send your question through the Q&A icon. As we have no further questions, I will return the floor to Mr. Fabio Schvartsman, the CEO of the company, for the closing remarks.

Fabio Schvartsman: Well, thank you so much for your time and attention. This is the first call that I take part in, and I would like to reinforce with you that what truly matters is that the company will do everything it needs to do to reach that position of financial balance. This, I think, has been demonstrated by the recent actions adopted by the company, the substitution of the leadership, the sale of assets, and the company is showing that it will act in a very rational way, in an appropriate way to face the problems. The great benefit that this company has is the quality of its assets, and they pose several alternatives for us.

We will work with them, and the company has a background, a very good relationship with its customers, with the financial system, and we will put this to good use to reach that balance. The company has shown to me that capacity to have a quick reaction and to change decisively to face the momentary difficulties, the difficulties due to the present-day scenario. In mining, we have a structural solution that is being built. It will be ready soon. In the other businesses, we do not have short-term problems. Quite the contrary, they all have more upsides than downsides, and we continue to have more good assets than anything else in the company.

You can count on me so that the company will do the necessary work going forward to present to you a better scenario, the best positive scenario. Thank you all for your attention.

Operator: Thank you. The earnings call for CSN ends here. Have a very good day.

#3040. Today, Voyager 1 Becomes the First Spacecraft a Full Light-Day From Home

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Voyager 1 has been flying at about 38,000 mph since 1980. This morning, that steady pace carries it a full light-day from home.

NASA’s Voyager 1 left Earth on Sept. 5, 1977, carrying a camera, a set of science instruments and a gold-plated record of sounds and images from home. Forty-nine years later, it’s reaching a distance no spacecraft has attained before: one light-day, or roughly 16.1 billion miles, from Earth. At that range, light needs a full 24 hours to make the trip between Earth and the probe.

At 5:16:07 a.m. ET on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach that light-day milestone. From that point on, a radio signal between the spacecraft and NASA’s Deep Space Network takes more than a day to travel in either direction.

NASA puts the journey at 49 years, two months and 11 days, counting from Voyager 1’s launch in September 1977. The probe still sends data home, though at a rate slower than dial-up, and NASA plans a live discussion with the Voyager team on Thursday to mark the occasion.

It’s quite an accomplishment for a spacecraft built in the mid-1970s. One light-day is the distance that light travels in a single day at the speed of light, which is approximately 186,282 miles per second. That translates to 25.9 billion kilometers or about 16.1 billion miles in a single day. At an average human walking speed of 3 mph, it would take a human 612,015 years to travel that distance on foot.

Fortunately, Voyager 1 has been traveling a bit faster. It currently zips through the cosmos at a steady 37,763 mph, a speed it achieved in 1980 after a gravity-assisted Saturn flyby. It has been flying at that speed ever since.

The milestone comes 14 years after Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the point where the sun’s heliosphere ends, and entered interstellar space. It’s also 28 years after the spacecraft passed Pioneer 10 to become the human-made object that has traveled the farthest into space.

NASA marked the milestone with a global Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day event on Tuesday evening. Just after sunset, the agency wanted people to head outside and point their smartphone or tablet lights skyward to spark a planet-wide wave of light as Earth rotates, much like fans doing the wave at a stadium.

The space agency also made a website for the occasion. The website is simple. It flashes Voyager’s VGR call sign in Morse code. If you want to try it, click the link, hit begin, and then point your phone or tablet screen at the sky. The website does all the work for you.

NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory will follow up on Thursday at noon ET with a moderated discussion on the milestone, featuring status updates on both Voyager probes and a live Q&A with reporters and audience members.

The historic milestone isn’t without its drama. Voyager 1 has been in space for nearly half a century, and in that time, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory has done everything it can to extend the spacecraft’s life. That includes troubleshooting issues, performing maintenance, and shutting down various systems to save power and extend the spacecraft’s lifespan.

Several of those efforts took place in 2026. The team running Voyager 1 spent weeks shutting down three devices and powering on three low-power alternatives to reduce overall power usage. This initiative, which was internally called the Big Bang, was also performed on Voyager 2. The transition was completed in early September, giving Voyager 1 more time with its dwindling power supply while also keeping it warm enough to continue operating in the frigid conditions of interstellar space.

It was a tricky maneuver that required the team to simultaneously turn multiple instruments on and off. The difficulty of the maneuver was amplified by the fact that it took almost a full day for a signal to reach Voyager and another full day for Voyager to send a signal back, with hours of downtime while the spacecraft performed the operations.

All of this took place several months after Voyager 1 experienced a sudden drop in power, which necessitated shutting off one of its three instruments still in operation. Voyager 1 now has only two operational instruments.

Making it a whole light-day away from Earth is likely going to be Voyager 1’s final milestone while it still has enough power to communicate with Earth. Voyager 1 is powered by three radioisotope thermoelectric generators. They are essentially nuclear-powered batteries that generate energy by converting the steady heat from decaying plutonium-238.

When Voyager 1 first launched, its radioisotope thermoelectric generators produced about 470 watts of power. But plutonium-238 doesn’t last forever, and after 50 years in space, those generators now produce about 215 watts of power, with an average loss of about 4 watts per year. Most of that power is used to keep Voyager 1 up and running, which is why NASA has shut down eight of the 10 instruments that Voyager had when it launched.

At its current rate of usage and decay, Voyager 1 is expected to shut down its final science instrument in the 2030s and will eventually lose communication with Earth in 2036 due to insufficient power to send back a radio signal.

The same fate is expected for Voyager 2, Voyager 1’s twin, which has also spent half a century in space. While it is labeled the sequel, Voyager 2 actually launched 16 days before Voyager 1, and the two have spent nearly identical amounts of time traversing the cosmos. Thanks to its slower speed and trajectory, it likely won’t reach the one light-day distance until after its instruments shut down.

Voyager 1 will lose all of its power before it hits its next milestone, which is the beginning of the Oort Cloud, a vast, icy shell of comets at the edge of our solar system. It’ll take about 300 years for Voyager 1 to make it there.

Thanks to the near-perfect vacuum of outer space, Voyager 1 will continue to fly at its current speed even after it shuts down entirely. So it’ll still hit that milestone; it just won’t be able to phone home to tell us about it.

#3039. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#3036. Which Laptops Last the Longest? Check Out the Laptops I’ve Tested With the Best Battery Life

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

As part of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I share laptop recommendations and explain why battery life surged in 2026.

I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re currently using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

With many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours!

This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

Plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

The biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

Apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

Intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life

Whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.

#3035. I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful

One thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:

With the repository added, you can install it with:

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few

It’s been a very long time since Canonical had a disappointing release, and 27.04 will keep up that trend.

#3034. TJX (TJX) Q3 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

While the company faced headwinds from higher freight and fuel costs, it maintained its full-year pre-tax profit margin guidance and raised its full-year revenue outlook. The company indicated that execution issues at the Marmaxx division are being addressed through additional oversight, with performance expected to continue improving through the holiday season. Management stated that the company is well-positioned for the fourth quarter with high liquidity to chase merchandise deals in a market currently loaded with quality branded goods.

I am very pleased with our overall third quarter results. Once again, sales, profitability, and earnings per share exceeded our expectations. Consolidated comp sales increased 4%, driven by continued strong comp sales growth at HomeGoods, TJX Canada, and TJX International, and we saw comp sales improvement at Marmaxx.

Importantly, we are expecting further improvement at Marmaxx in the fourth quarter. We are very pleased with the overall progress we have made at Marmaxx and believe the execution issues will be largely behind us by the end of the year. We believe our third quarter consolidated results demonstrate the benefit of our global business and diversified portfolio of retail banners. We are confident in our plans for the holiday season and have many initiatives to drive traffic and sales underway. Reconciliations detailing the net impact of these items on our results can be found in today's press release and on the investor section of our website.

Marmaxx's adjusted segment profit margin was 13.8%, down 110 basis points versus last year, primarily driven by higher freight and fuel costs. At our Sierra stores, we are happy with the sales we are seeing as we expand that chain across the U.S. At our U.S. e-commerce sites, we continue to expand categories and add new brands for our online shoppers. We are pleased to see sales improvement at Marmaxx, and we are confident in our near and long-term growth plans for our largest division.
