#2992. Preventing Data Loss, At Scale

Christian Stegh, CTO and VP of Strategy at eGroup Enabling Technologies.

​Data loss prevention tools have spiked in popularity since the arrival of enterprise AI. But even though tools exist to protect enterprise data, operating them is far from foolproof. CISOs have good reason to deploy tools to protect their corporate assets. Oversharing and over-permissioned data can lead to leakage, and the average cost of an insider security incident is $19.5 million, dwarfing the average ransomware payment of $139,000.​ This article outlines lessons learned from six years of enterprise experience rolling out common DLP products like Varonis and Microsoft Purview.​​

Two legitimate concerns about data are consistent:

1. Enterprise AI tools like Copilot can search and find any unprotected data within the enterprise to which that user has access.

2. Confidential corporate data may be uploaded to public AI tools, which, unless turned off, use the input to train their models by default.

To reduce these risks, organizations are investing in tools. Those that are succeeding add user adoption and process improvements to the equation.

There are myriad challenges of successfully adopting DLP tools at scale, but four common themes arise.

3. Little time or interest from the business to change behavior.

4. Inadequate resources to operate DLP systems at scale.

The first two are closely related. For most organizations, people have created, shared and stored data with little consideration about its life cycle or protection. Relatively few organizations can answer, “How many sensitive documents are stored in which locations?” For some, simply defining what data is sensitive is challenging! Without awareness of the scope of the sprawl, there’s no shared understanding of the severity of the risk, and no sustained action.

No matter the type of business, challenge three, business resistance to change, is ubiquitous. Business leaders rarely see value in interrupting their work for DLP. DLP has been IT’s job.

Speaking of IT’s job, that’s challenge number four, and a common question: Should operating DLP be a full-time job? DLP tools create false positives and need tuning to scale. CISA recommends a maintenance process with “recurring activity with tasks scheduled monthly, semiannually, and annually.” Tasking an already at-capacity SecOps team with more alerts can create a shock to the support team, halting rollouts before they scale.

Use simple frameworks for data classification. Varonis suggests three classes, and Microsoft between three and five classes (i.e., public, internal, confidential, secret).

Getting the business to agree on a framework is easier in organizations where data is sacred. Take for instance, health insurance and benefits provider PlanSource, who implemented four classes of data. Since they administer benefits programs for employees of 1,000 organizations, their CISO, Tony Spurlin, is on high alert. “We are a data company, and what comes with data is a significant amount of trust. You have one chance with trust. You break it once and that’s it.”​

It’s challenging to begin the DLP journey by labeling and protecting the organization’s niche, proprietary data, even if it’s truly the most sensitive. Agreeing on how to handle it and who needs access isn’t straightforward.

A simpler step is to start with data everyone agrees should be protected, like employees’ personally identifiable or health information. That’s simpler to scan and protect, and there’s no argument that it needs protection. Next, protect complex data like intellectual property, customer content and unique identifiers.

Auto-labeling sounds great in the marketing slides. So it may sound counterintuitive to suggest that people start by manually classifying their own files. Consider the upsides, though. Manually labeling helps people build their data literacy (solving problem #1 above). Plus, manual labeling is possible with the less expensive Purview license, unlike the upgrade needed to auto-label data. Later, once people understand the process, label all that at-rest data.

There’s no question that user acceptance leads to ROI, but how do you make people care about a dry topic like labeling files? It’s about awareness of the need to change, as well as the tactical how-tos. This philosophy is backed up by SANS, who not only stresses the “why” but how to implement a strong feedback loop. Looping back to suggestion one: By protecting employees’ own information first, you’ll get more support for the larger initiative.

The rollout of any DLP solution is iterative, and vendor marketecture can set some misleading expectations. Microsoft’s Purview deployment guide calls for five weeks of setup but notes that the time to “operate, expand and retroactive options” is “situational.” Gartner Group analyst Mike Huskey said, “Yes, you could ‘deploy’ Purview in 6 weeks, or in an afternoon, if you just want to click buttons.”

To scale anything but the simplest rollout, plan for six-plus months. If you plan ahead and set up data literacy and milestones up front, things can move quickly. If planning, data literacy and milestones are set up front, as done at Verdantas, things can move “This is not a 12-month or 18-month project, but is something that you can do pretty quickly,” said CIO Sujan Turlapaty.

#2990. Top Wall Street analysts suggest these 3 dividend stocks for consistent income

Inflation data, earnings reports and tensions in the Middle East have been influencing the market. In this volatile backdrop, investors seeking income can bolster their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

The recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help inform investors in their search for attractive stocks from the vast universe of dividend-paying companies. These experts assign ratings after analyzing a company's financials and ability to consistently pay dividends while also seeking capital appreciation.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Integrated oil and gas giant Exxon Mobil has increased its dividends for 43 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.03 per share (annualized dividend of $4.12), XOM stock offers a yield of 2.6%.

In his latest research report on energy players, Morgan Stanley analyst Devin McDermott reiterated a buy rating on Exxon Mobil stock and increased his price target to $177 from $168.

The analyst raised his free cash flow estimates to reflect Q2 guidance and the oil price strip, with the largest increase noted for integrated players due to higher refining margins. Notably, the five-star analyst raised his cash flow estimates by an average of 20% for the second half of 2026 and 7% for 2027.

McDermott highlighted that while pure-play refiners have rallied on stronger margins, integrated energy stocks have lagged, creating relative-value opportunities in major North American integrated producers, including Exxon Mobil, Suncor and Cenovus Energy.

Overall, McDermott is bullish on Exxon Mobil, as he expects the company to deliver strong earnings and cash flow growth, driven by robust upstream volumes, high-value projects in Product Solutions, and more than $5 billion of additional structural cost savings.

"XOM's large global integrated operations and strong balance sheet (0.0x 2027 net leverage) make it a clear defensive play in an uncertain macro backdrop," said McDermott.

McDermott ranks No. 726 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.80%. See Exxon Mobil Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

Moving on to natural gas producer Expand Energy. The company announced a quarterly base dividend of $0.575 per share to be paid on Sept. 3. At an annualized dividend of $2.30 per share, EXE offers a yield of about 2.3%.

Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reaffirmed a buy rating on Expand Energy stock and increased his price target to $113 from $99. Mehta attributed his higher price target to cash flow improvement and a strong outlook for shareholder returns. He also cited the stock's attractive valuation, with an 11% free cash flow, or FCF, yield based on his 2027/2028 estimates compared with the peer average of 9%.

The five-star analyst expects Expand Energy to generate FCF per share of about $10 in FY28, up from the prior estimate of about $8 at his mid-cycle price forecast of $3.50/MMBtu Henry Hub. Mehta raised his FCF estimate to reflect an improved outlook for share repurchases, operational efficiencies, and gas pricing realizations.

Furthermore, the analyst expects the recently announced $1.25 billion Twin Eagle acquisition to enhance the competitive positioning of the combined business to expand to premium markets and capture incremental deals in the power and LNG end markets.

Mehta ranks No. 449 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.1%. See Expand Energy Insider Trading on TipRanks.

Mehta is also bullish on Diamondback Energy, an independent oil and natural gas company focused on energy reserves that are primarily in the Permian Basin in West Texas. The company recently paid a base cash dividend of $1.10 per share for the second quarter of 2026. FANG stock offers a dividend yield of 2.2%.

Mehta increased his price target on FANG stock to $220 from $212 and reiterated a buy rating, citing the company's capital-efficient volume growth as oil prices remain high amid persistent supply disruption in the Middle East.

"We remain constructive on FANG, a high-quality, pure-play Permian Basin operator that continues to drive incremental capital efficiencies and strong well productivity relative to peers," said Mehta.

Also, the analyst said that the removal of a minimum return of capital commitment gives Diamondback more flexibility in taking capital allocation decisions amid high oil price volatility and macro uncertainty.

Mehta added that Diamondback sees a favorable environment for production growth, driven by the potential need for global inventory restocking. He highlighted that during Q2 2026, FANG's production volumes of 1,018 Mboe/d exceeded the high end of the company's guidance, driven by a stronger-than-expected natural gas output from Barnett development and improved downstream gas marketing.

Overall, Mehta is optimistic about Diamondback's growth and sees more upside in the stock, given higher production estimates, solid productivity and a deepening position in the Barnett shale formation. See Diamondback Energy Financials on TipRanks.

Hyatt is updating its rewards program in 2027, and it means you'll earn Milestone Rewards even sooner than before.

Editor/Content Strategist & Smart Travel Podcast Host

It’s going to be easier to rack up extra benefits if you’re a frequent Hyatt customer in 2027. World of Hyatt announced new Milestone Rewards, the ability to stack awards (such as Free Night Certificates and Suite Upgrade Awards) on a single stay and a simpler 365-day expiration on all awards.

The news expands on the fresh details revealed Nov. 17, 2026, around World of Hyatt’s partnership with Delta SkyMiles, which was first announced in September.

The additions to the Milestone Rewards are designed to give members more choice and personalization, according to Laurie Blair, senior vice president of global marketing and loyalty at Hyatt.

"We’re shaping the future of World of Hyatt around what our members value most. After a year of listening, one thing is clear: members want more distinctive benefits, more freedom to use their awards and the opportunity to choose awards that matter most to them,” Blair said in an email to NerdWallet.

But top-tier Globalist members will soon have to choose between perks that they previously received automatically. Most notably, Globalists will no longer receive free parking on award nights in 2027. Instead, they can choose a Free Parking Award as a Milestone Reward that they can apply to award or paid stays.

The Delta Air Lines and Hyatt partnership will also mainly benefit frequent flyers and hotel guests. With the exception of the limited-time intro promotion, only Delta or Hyatt members with elite status will earn points in both programs. Hyatt elites will have to purchase premium tickets on Delta — not economy — to earn Hyatt points on the flight.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, World of Hyatt will extend Milestone Rewards to guests who have not yet qualified for the first level of elite status. Southwest Airlines did the same in its recent revamp to give loyal customers a thank you before they’ve reached any level of elite status.

World of Hyatt members will reach the first Milestone Reward at just 10 nights or 20,000 Base Points. Previously, it was 20 nights or 35,000 Base Points.

The reward choices at the first milestone are:

A tier-qualifying night credit, which gets you closer to the next level of elite status.

A $25 FIND Experience credit (Hyatt’s platform for local experiences such as cooking classes).

A $30 spa credit good at Hyatt Inclusive Collection resorts.

The latter two will likely still require you to pay money out of pocket to use them, as the credit will only cover a portion of your bill. For example, the cheapest spa treatment at Secrets Playa Mujeres Golf & Spa Resort in Cancun, Mexico, will still run you $109 (or $79 after the credit).

The Milestone Rewards start to get good at the higher tiers. Starting at 20 nights, you can select from the existing Milestone Rewards, as well as new items. Some of the new options include:

Free parking on award nights is going away as a Globalist tier benefit. In 2027, a Free Parking Award will be an option that Globalists can select at the 60, 70, 80 and 90 nights The parking award can be used on either a qualifying award or paid stay for up to seven nights.

Hyatt said in a call with NerdWallet that roughly 70% of Globalists weren’t using the free parking benefit at all.

Globalists who have earned status in 2026 for 2027 will be grandfathered into the automatic free parking on award stays through their tier expiration date in February 2028.

To use these new awards, the Hyatt booking process is also getting an upgrade. Previously, awards like Suite Upgrade Awards and Free Night Awards couldn’t be redeemed on the same stay. Starting in 2027, members can combine eligible awards on a single reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and Free Parking Awards.

The new booking system will also make it easier to pay for some nights of a single reservation with awards, points, cash or a combination of points and cash.

Every award earned going forward will also carry a 365-day expiration from the date it’s issued, replacing the patchwork of different validity windows. Previously, Suite Upgrade and Guest of Honor Awards expired at “rest of year plus 14 days,” which was just a tad confusing. Meanwhile, Free Night Awards earned through Milestone Rewards were valid for 180 days from the date of issuance, which was not a lot of time to plan a trip.

The Milestone Rewards kick in next year, but the other big change around the Delta partnership is available now.

Hyatt elite members can earn World of Hyatt Bonus Points on eligible Delta flights (Delta Comfort, Premium Select, First Class and Delta One). Basic Economy or standard Main Cabin fares will earn nothing from this partnership at all.

Discoverist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $2 spent.

Explorist, Globalist and Lifetime Globalist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $1 spent.

Delta Medallion members (Silver through Diamond) can earn 1 Delta mile per $1 spent at participating Hyatt properties, on top of their regular Hyatt points.

Even if you don’t have elite status with either program, it’s still worth linking accounts to take advantage of the upcoming bonus point promotions:

Those who link their accounts and complete a qualifying Hyatt stay from Nov. 17 to Dec. 31, 2026, will earn one bonus Tier-Qualifying Night Credit.

A second bonus point offer runs Jan. 4 through Feb. 15, 2027, for members who take their first Delta flight or Hyatt stay after linking their accounts. Members will earn 1,000 Delta SkyMiles after the Hyatt stay or 1,000 Hyatt points after their first flight in a premium cabin on Delta.

Hyatt and Delta are also holding a sweepstakes through Nov. 23 — no points or miles required to enter — for a free three-night trip for two at Alila Mayakoba in Riviera Maya, Mexico, plus two $1,000 Delta gift cards. Linking your accounts before entering gets you a bonus entry.

If you are interested in dual accrual in 2027, there are some routes to elite status through travel credit cards. Hyatt’s entry-level elite tier comes as a benefit of holding the World of Hyatt Credit Card, but Discoverists earn Hyatt points at half the rate of Explorist and Globalist elites on premium Delta fares.

#2987. Target’s Shoppers Are Coming Back as Store Traffic Jumps 5% After Falling 2.2% a Year Ago. Can the Momentum Last?

Target stock is up 74% this year. Can it keep rallying?

By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:09PM EST

You may have missed it from all the attention on AI stocks this year, but Target (TGT +4.01%) is one of the best-performing stocks in the S&P 500.

The retail giant has jumped 74% year-to-date as it's put its earlier struggles behind it and returned to growth under new CEO Michael Fiddelke.

Target kept that momentum going in the third quarter as the stock jumped 6.7% Wednesday on another strong earnings report.

The retailer easily beat estimates on the top and bottom lines, as comparable sales jumped 5.6% on a 5% increase in traffic, showing shoppers are returning to its stores. That drove revenue up 7.1% to $27.07 billion, which topped the consensus at $26.54 billion.

The company's Fun 101 category, which includes products like toys, electronics, sports, and entertainment, delivered 27% growth. Beauty and food and beverage were also strong, up 9% and 7%, respectively. Target's non-retail business, including subscriptions like Target Circle 360, the Target+ marketplace, and its Roundel ad business, grew nearly 20%, showing the playbook that it's borrowed from Amazon and Walmart is paying off.

Further down the income statement, Target's gross margin rose 120 basis points to 29.4%, excluding a benefit from tariff refunds, as operating leverage from the increase in comparable sales helped drive gross margin improvement. Adjusted operating margin rose from 4.4% to 5.2%, excluding the tariff benefit, and adjusted earnings per share jumped from $1.78 to $2.65, or $2.15 excluding a $0.50 benefit from related tariff refunds, representing a 21% gain. That beat estimates at $2.07.

Target also raised its full-year revenue growth from 5% to 6%, and its adjusted EPS guidance from $9.90-$10.90 to $10.65-$11.40, which helps explain today's pop as well.

With Target stock nearly doubling this year, investors are clearly betting on a long-term recovery, but is the momentum sustainable? Let's take a look at what's going well for the company.

On some level, Target is benefiting from the low-hanging fruit in front of it after several years of underperforming its industry. The company is reclaiming lost market share with basic improvements like reducing out-of-stocks and investing more in labor and training to improve the sales experience. The strong comparable sales in part reflect the previous downturn in the business as the company recoups lost sales.

The retailer is also getting back to its roots with collaborations with brands like Pokémon that have helped drive its success in Fun 101, and price cuts have helped drive traffic without hurting margins.

Unlike in the second quarter, Target did not report growth in all of its core merchandising categories, as sales of apparel and accessories fell, and home furnishings sales were nearly flat, reflecting broader pressure in the housing sector. Fiddelke said he was not satisfied with the company's performance.

Target's implied fourth-quarter guidance should be encouraging to investors coming during the crucial holiday season.

While the third-quarter results weren't perfect given the misses in some core merchandising categories, Target is still performing well in a challenging retail environment, and the company is finding its way back to its historical formula of success. Meanwhile, the growth in the non-retail business is encouraging and should continue.

Trading at a price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 15.5 based on its updated guidance for the year, Target looks well-priced. While there's still some risk in the stock as the company picks through the low-hanging fruit, the risk/reward looks attractive at the current price given its momentum and the potential to further claw back lost sales and margin.

#2985. Top Wall Street analysts like these 3 stocks for the long haul

Global stock markets have been volatile as investors assess high bond yields and continued tensions between the U.S. and Iran. There are concerns about the impact of uncertainty in the Middle East on oil prices and consequently on inflation.

Investors who prefer to look beyond short-term noise and buy stocks with attractive long-term growth potential can follow the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. The ratings of these experts are backed by in-depth research of a company's financials and thorough analysis of the factors affecting its business performance.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA) reported stellar fiscal second-quarter results and reassured investors about continued strength in AI-driven demand for its chips. Moreover, Nvidia's FY28 revenue growth outlook of 70% was well above the Street's expectations.

Reacting to the Q2 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reiterated a buy rating on NVDA and increased his price target to $300 from $288. "This is our Top Pick in the semis group, with a compelling product cycle, exceptional growth and valuation below peers," said the 5-star analyst.

Nvidia delivered impressive quarterly results despite supply constraints, Moore said, but he believes that the FY28 revenue and gross margin commentary mattered more, with a favorable outlook for both measures.

Moore said Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance for FY28 was above his own estimate of 52% and the consensus of about 40%. The top-line growth estimate was a "remarkable figure" given supply issues and Moore said he expects Nvidia to continue to address bottlenecks to deliver rapid growth.

Among other takeaways, the analyst said performance metrics for Vera Rubin chips were strong, with Nvidia emphasizing a 30x higher throughput per megawatt and 35x lower token cost compared with Grace Blackwell Ultra.

Moore ranks No. 159 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 60% of the time, delivering an average return of 24.60%. See Nvidia Statistics on TipRanks.

Ride-hailing and delivery platform Uber Technologies (UBER) was recommended by BMO Capital analyst Brian Pitz, who discussed the company's opportunity in the autonomous vehicle (AV) market in a recent research note that reiterated a buy rating and price target of $119.

The 5-star analyst highlighted Uber's transition into a diversified marketplace, with investors now focusing on its AV growth prospects. The key question is how much value can Uber generate as AVs become commercialized, Pitz asked.

"We continue to believe that Uber's AV strategy is evolving and will become a significant driver of revenue and profitability," the analyst said.

Importantly, Pitz believes that Uber can establish itself as a preferred mobility platform for AV makers, supported by its growing AV infrastructure capabilities and an expanding partner base. This would enable Uber to win a significant share of value as the AV market is commercialized.

Additionally, Pitz noted Uber's enhanced position in the AV value chain, with the company shifting from serving as a distribution channel for robotaxis to becoming a broader platform for AV mobility. The analyst discussed Uber's efforts to capture growth opportunities in the AV market, including higher capital spending, expansion into new markets and building partnerships beyond Alphabet's Waymo.

Pitz ranks No. 574 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of about 12.20%. See Uber Technologies Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the second quarter of FY27. But the company's increased FY28 guidance fell short of investors' high expectations.

In reaction to the Q2 FY27 results, KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reaffirmed a buy rating on Marvell Technology, with a price target of $400. The analyst noted that Marvell's results and outlook were driven by strength in its data center business. The Q2 FY27 data center business grew 46% year-over-year, to $2.17 billion, far above KeyBanc's estimate of $2.09 billion.

Management "highlighted accelerating AI networking demand across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up architectures, supported by strong 800G optical DSP demand, rapid 1.6T ramp, broader 51.2T switch deployments and higher TIA/driver demand," Vinh said.

Consequently, Marvell raised its data center revenue guidance, now expecting 60% growth in FY27 and more than 60% in FY28.

Regarding the recently announced $120 billion warrant arrangement with Google, Vinh said management argued that programs tied to the warrant are already priced into the custom outlook through FY28. Meanwhile, new programs and those in execution are expected to drive significant upside to the previous FY29 custom XPU revenue estimate of over $10 billion, Vinh said, citing management.

Vinh ranks No. 123 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 60% of the time, delivering an average return of 28.50%. See Marvell Technology Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

We draw against this $1 million over time against 70% of our acquisition spend each month.

As each cohort comes in for that month that was funded, General Catalyst will receive 70% of the gross profit associated with that cohort each month as those subscriptions renew until they have recovered their principal, and then depending on how long it takes them to recover that principal, they will receive a defined premium on top of that principal. After the principal's repaid is when that premium is actually paid. What that premium is, if we look at the next slide, it depends on the speed of the payback. Once the principal plus the premium has been paid for a cohort, General Catalyst's participation in that particular cohort ends, at which point then all the profit from those cohorts is ours, and it had been pre-funded in a strong cash flow sort of way. This structure allows us to fund the portion of acquisition investment with the future receipts each cohort's intended to generate. Also a reminder, this financing is non-dilutive. This cost of the financing is really just this premium share that we are laying out here on the right side. That is the only cost of it.

On the cash flow statement, you will see this coming as cash from financing.

As it relates to adjusted free cash flow, which is a non-IFRS metric, this is our operating cash flow, which in the quarter is negative $27.5 million, net of CapEx, which brought to zero in the quarter, plus the GC funding of cash, which is that $31.6 million of inflow, which puts our adjusted free cash flow for the quarter at $4.1 million positive, and our ending cash balance that increased for the quarter. Let us turn to the balance sheet and look at that real quick. September ended with $111 million of cash and current financial assets, up from $109.4 million at the end of Q2.

That total comprises of $63.4 million of cash and cash equivalents and $48 million of current financial assets. Inventories increased to $20.1 million compared with $14 million at the end of Q2. We also separately increased deposits and supplier prepayments with our manufacturers to prepare for the holiday quarter and the products planned for next year. The balance sheet contains the $34.7 million of borrowings under the General Catalyst agreement, as we saw in the last slide. For the first quarter of availability, the partnership really performed exactly as we intended it to.

We were able to grow cash balance in a quarter when, one, we spent a record marketing investment to acquire our largest quarterly customer cohort we have ever had, and two, significantly bolster our inventory reserves in prep for a big Q4 and into next year, especially with some new product launches. Next, let us turn to our outlook. We are reaffirming our full year 2026 total revenue guidance of $220 million-$230 million, including IM8 revenue of $215 million-$222 million. Subtracting the nine months as reported from those figures, the fourth quarter works out to approximately $73 million-$83 million for the group and $73 million-$80 million for IM8.

We expect a second half adjusted EBITDA loss of $30 million-$35 million, compared with a negative $8 million-$12 million range that we gave back in August, as Danny mentioned. With that $12.7 million in Q3, the range implies a fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $17 million-$22 million. This loss is bigger in terms of dollars, but as a percent of revenue, it actually improves from 31% in the first half to 23% in the second half at the midpoint of our guidance. Within the second half, more of it falls in the fourth quarter, about 25% of revenue as an adjusted EBITDA loss versus 20% adjusted EBITDA loss in Q3.

This is deliberate increase in customer acquisition spend that we're planning. Under two years, the next 91,000 customers are at 2.7 times, and those will pass the 3.0 mark by early 2027. CAC has also declined two straight quarters, as we mentioned, and we will look to continue investing in Q4 for the same reason, for as long as our returns will hold. We expect adjusted free cash flow to remain positive in Q4 again, despite the negative operating cash flow due to the General Catalyst financing. We're also affirming IM8's annualized revenue run rate to hit at least $300 million by year end.

Our operational investment focus for Q4 is deliver against the demand while preparing for our exciting product launches that we mentioned earlier. For 2027, we're reiterating our revenue guidance for IM8 to $400 million or more on the current product catalog. This includes no revenue from hydration, Care Bears, other products, retail, or China. All of that is outside of the current guidance. Of course, as Danny Yeung showed, that forecast, none of it is earned. We have to remain focused on retention, efficient acquisition, and execution across the year. Lastly, for the first time, we're publishing a long-term financial framework.

This is a question I get asked a lot about, what does the business, as it matures, start to look like from a margin standpoint? I thought this would be really helpful to show. Over time, we'll be targeting a gross margin of 70%-75%. We'll be targeting operating costs of 8%-12%. Brand royalty and ambassador costs should drop to 3%-5%, and our acquisition marketing should drop to 35%-50%, which would put you to an adjusted EBITDA margin of 15%-25% for the business as it matures. You can see just through the progression in 2026 that we're well on our way towards these numbers.

Still quite a bit of work to do, and none of this is guidance, and we don't have a set timeline on any of this, but this is what you should be looking for us to be moving towards on all these lines. Gross margin in particular, we've onboarded a new third-party manufacturer in Q3. They will come online in Q1. With that, we're going to be adding additional capacity and lower production costs, so our gross margin is expected to improve in the early part of 2027. We're not yet ready to say specifically what the guidance for gross margin will be yet in Q1. Look for some of that next quarter.

She is an important part of our build-out, and you can expect us to continue adding experienced U.S. leadership in the coming quarters. Thank you to all of our Prenetics and IM8 teams for their tireless support, and thanks to all of you for joining us today. I will give it back to Danny now for closing remarks, and then we will open it up for questions.

A brand that is getting stronger every month, a partner financing 70% of what we spend on acquiring customers, and data that shows what every cohort returns. What we'll do, we'll be able to utilize AI to identify the winners very fast. When we do identify winners, we'll then show these same ads on AppLovin, on X, on Snap, on TikTok, the same aspects. I think that we would be shooting for the upper range eventually, but the lower end is clearer in sight right now.

Operator: Thank you, George. Our next question comes from Kyle Bauser of Titan. Kyle, please go ahead.

Kyle Bauser: Great. Thanks for all the updates here. My first question is around price elasticity and any kind of competitive dynamics. You've obviously taken significant share from the top players, and we also saw that 87% of new IM8 customers had no observed purchase from AG1, Grüns, or Thorne before their first IM8 order. Just how have the pricing competitive dynamics been out there? Obviously, you've got a premium price on yours given the superior product, but should we expect continued pricing stability?

Danny Yeung: Yeah, I mean, we haven't seen much price issues for us. I mean, again, we haven't changed our pricing since we've I mean, actually, since we've launched, we've actually had a slight price increase, but we haven't seen any issues in terms of price elasticity or any type of demand, as you see evidenced by the continued growth on a quarterly basis.

Kyle Bauser: Got it. Maybe just around the clinical trials, can you talk a little bit more about how this might be unlocking new segments of the population? Obviously, consumers are getting much smarter, and awareness is certainly building. Do you anticipate results driving kind of new cohorts of consumers or

Speaker 4: I'm a brand manager, and my ClickUp looks like this. I'm a project manager. My ClickUp looks like this. I'm a product manager, and my ClickUp looks like this.

Danny Yeung: that consumer. We will be able to leverage that in terms of marketing. A lot of marketing and also, like you mentioned, clinicians will be able to prescribe it much more. Very, very positive and hopeful about these trials that are going to be releasing in the first half of 2027.

Kyle Bauser: Excellent. Well, thanks for all the updates.

Operator: Thank you, Kyle. Our last question comes from Alex Hantman of Sidoti. Alex, please go ahead.

Alex Hantman: Thank you, thanks for taking questions. I just wanted to start with repeat orders. They were looking great, 59% of customer billing this quarter. I am curious, as that share grows, how quickly does acquisition marketing come down towards your 35%-50% range, what does that mean for the timing of profitability?

Brian Rosin: Yeah, so the 59% is nice to see. However, if we can continue to invest at the three to one, we would rather keep spending more and more into new customers. So it is a conundrum in that when we spend more on customer acquisition, your percent of new revenue is higher, but that is a great sign for the future with the returns that we have. So, I would again say that profitability is not necessarily a goal. It is inevitable with the math that eventually it just becomes too hard to outrun it, as I mentioned a little bit ago.

So, it is hard to put a timeline on it because we have exceeded kind of where I would have expected us to have been able to spend up to at a CAC that is declining. If that continues, then of course we will continue to do that, at which point you push profitability out. If we start to slow to spend, it brings profitability forward in the nearer term. It is too tricky to try to say specifically when that will happen because we have been exceeding what I would have thought we could have been spending. Again, with new products and all that, we do not know how those are going to impact CAC.

We do not know how it is going to impact overall LTVs and LTRs. We need to get these products launched before we will be able to kind of model into the future more specifically around profitability target. I would expect that the marketing will continue to come down as a percentage of sales, which we saw it already from Q2 to Q3. I would expect that to trend mostly down. There might be some blips here and there, but mostly that will keep trending down to that range that we gave for longer term.

Alex Hantman: Okay, helpful context. Thank you. Speaking of new products, I know IM8 Hydration launches into about 160,000 active subscriptions. It is a big number. I am curious what attach rate would you consider a success in year one if you have a target, and also about how margins might compare to the core products?

Brian Rosin: Alex, from a margin standpoint, just to touch on the margin of those. The margin profile will be very similar to our current business margin, from a product cost standpoint, for sure. From a logistics standpoint, it depends on if we can trade people into a multi-month, or a bigger basket size and attach, whether it is our current products or an Essentials bundle. Or if you are getting a three-month supply of Hydration, for example, that will allow the margin to keep really in line with where we are today.

If we are seeing AOV start to decline, because people are taking more of the one-month supply of Hydration, which is a lower price point out the door than our current assortment, you might see a little bit of margin pressure just on the fulfillment side alone. It costs us more or less the same to ship a product to a consumer if they buy $50 worth as if they pay $100. You will see a bit of pressure potentially, depending on how AOV looks. We will be trying it on the DTC channel for sure to get people into a multipack, which would alleviate that pressure entirely. The retail piece is also the other unknown there.

The retail channel looks different from a margin profile, as you can imagine. Much lower cost on the fulfillment side, much lower cost on the actual ad dollars specific going into retail. As I model it out, I think the margin of the total new products will be very unchanged versus the current. There is going to be some pluses and minuses there, but overall, I would not expect it to be pressured much.

Alex Hantman: Very helpful. Thanks for the color. Last one from us. I know we have spoken about retail at length, but the 2027 bridge also includes about $19 million from marketplace and B2B. I know that is only about 5% of revenue, but I wanted to hear a little bit more about the B2B opportunity looks like and how fast perhaps that could grow from your perspective.

Danny Yeung: Yeah. On the marketplace aspect is like Amazon, B2B, we actually have a lot of other businesses reaching out to us as part of their wellness aspects. Again, it is still a small part of our overall business if you consider next year we are forecasting $400 million. I think the focus will still remain DTC and then retail, and then B2B and marketplace, these are more like ad hoc opportunities that we will pick up.

Alex Hantman: Great. Thank you very much.

Operator: Thank you, Alex. That concludes our question and answer session. I will now turn the call back over to Danny for brief closing remarks.

Danny Yeung: Great. Thank you so much, everyone, for tuning in today. Hopefully it was very insightful. As I mentioned, we have a very detailed shareholder letter and investor deck, that we just pushed online. Yeah, I mean, again, going back to summary-wise, this quarter is another record quarter. We are heading into 2027 with a lot of strength. The revenues are growing, the cash position is growing, our cohorts are growing, with new products. It is very clear to us, at least from a business perspective, that we are reaching stronger momentum on a quarterly and on a monthly basis. Yeah, so we cannot be more excited about where the business is headed.

So, thank you, everyone, for tuning in, and look forward to chatting with everyone in the next quarter.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates eased today, but borrowing costs are still expensive for many homebuyers.

Mortgage rates are lower today, but recent averages above 7% are still eating into buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 21 basis points lower than yesterday and 13 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

#2979. ZTO Express (ZTO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Retail parcel volume surged 57% as the company prioritized quality over scale.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:14PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

ZTO Express (ZTO -0.39%) reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Management reported that the company focused on its "two-high, one-low" strategy, prioritizing high-quality market share and high-quality service while maintaining low end-to-end costs. The company reported parcel volume growth of 7% and an expansion of market share to 20.1% in a decelerating industry environment. Management stated that competition is transitioning to a quality-first development track supported by regulatory guidance. The company noted that its retail parcel volume grew 57%, contributing to an improved average selling price and earnings quality.

Operator: Please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sophie Li, Director of Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Sophie Li: Thank you, June. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. The company's results and the investor relations presentation were released earlier today and are available on the company's IR website at ir.zto.com. On the call today from ZTO are Mr. Meisong Lai, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and [Ms.] Huiping Yan, Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Lai will give a brief overview of the company's business operations and highlights, followed by [Ms.] Yan, who will go through the financials and guidance. They will both be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows.

I remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Such statements are based on management's current expectations and current market and operating conditions, and relate to events that involve known or unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors, all of which are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond the company's control, which may cause the company's actual results, performance, or achievements to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements. Further information regarding this and other risks, uncertainties, and factors is included in the company's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The company does not undertake any obligation to update any forward-looking statements as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise, except as required under law. It is now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Meisong Lai. Mr. Lai will read through his prepared remarks in their entirety in Chinese before I translate for him in English. [Non-English content].

Sophie Li: Thank you, Chairman Lai. Please allow me to translate first. Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining today's conference call. In the third quarter of 2026, industry parcel volume growth decelerated to 2.9% year-over-year as anti-involution policies continued to gain traction. Even though prices in a few regions fluctuated, the overall competitive landscape is gradually normalizing, and the industry is steadily moving towards quality-first development. ZTO extended the positive momentum of the first half of the year across our core operating metrics in this third quarter. Parcel volume reached 10.24 billion, up 7% year-over-year, and the market share rose 0.7 percentage points to 20.1%, further solidifying our leadership position. Operating profit was CNY 2.98 billion, up 23.8% year-over-year.

Adjusted net income was CNY 2.57 billion, up 2.6% year-over-year, as operating efficiency and earnings quality continued to improve. Retail parcel volume grew 57% year-over-year. The expansion of our high-value and diversified product and services not only added incremental volume but also enriched the source of income for our couriers. Oil prices remained at a relatively high level this quarter. Through deeper implementation of end-to-end digitalization and lean ops, we lowered the combined unit cost of transportation and sorting by CNY 0.02 year-over-year. Cost productivity was consistently harnessed. This result would not have been possible without the strong policy support, disciplined execution of our overall strategy, continuous improvements in operating efficiency, and the strong foundational support of our network.

Above all, the concerted efforts by all of our frontline partners, including couriers. Anti-involution has been evolving from a policy guidance to an industry consensus. Industry competition is shifting from simply trading price for volume to a high-quality development track that prioritizes economic sense that encompasses both quantity and quality. For the past three quarters, ZTO has been focusing on three priorities: high-quality market share, high-quality service, and low end-to-end costs. We continue to refine volume incentives and profit-sharing mechanisms to foster a fair, transparent eco-network that is built on shared success and relies on long-term operational efficiencies to achieve quality and economic returns.

By rolling out direct sorting and delivery and direct linkage network-wide, we have steadily achieved increases in home delivery capability, high-value parcel volume, and the earnings of outlets and couriers. Looking ahead, ZTO will further deepen the implementation of our two-high, one-low strategy and pursue profitable growth with unwavering commitment. First, take the lead in safeguarding a fair competitive environment. We will adhere to regulatory guidance, accurately ascertain market baseline and customer needs, effectively balance priorities and trade-offs. Proactively cultivate high-quality customers, keep optimizing our volume mix, and pursue premium market share. Second, continue to enhance service quality. We will further streamline pickup, sorting, line-haul transportation, and delivery. Maximize resource utilization while guarantee on-time delivery.

Align with platform service requirements and metrics to strengthen our pickup and delivery capabilities. Refine customer segmentation while continuing to iterate our product offerings, turning service reputation into differentiated brand perception and price premium. Third, deepen end-to-end cost reduction and efficiency gain. We will continue to optimize line-haul transportation and sortation efficiency, coordinate equipment installation by the outlets, enhance pickup and delivery cost control mechanisms, and drive quality and efficiency gains across the entire chain and at every stage, especially at the last mile, to help address industry challenges. Fourth, strengthen our network foundation by protecting frontline interests.

We will proactively provide support to outlets and safeguard couriers' rightful earnings and interests, empower outlets according to their different performance levels, ensure data integrity, and keep the feedback channels open. Maintain bottom lines for safety and compliance. We will guide outlets and couriers to steadily optimize product and income mix, and while continuing to strengthen service and product capabilities, actively broaden business inflow channels, laying a solid foundation for coordinated growth in market share, quality, and profit next year. ZTO has always held to a balanced approach that integrates quality, volume, and profitability, while practicing a shared success philosophy. We regard platform, outlets, and couriers as one community of shared interests.

As we further our mission of bringing happiness to more people through our services, not only are we evolving and growing the platform to be bigger and stronger, we are also committed to build equity and fairness for stability across our network. Backed by the robust infrastructure, financial strength, technological innovation, and digitization empowerment we have built over two decades, we are confident that in the face of new challenges as well as opportunities, we are able to unify perspectives with all of our partners, advance the steady implementation of the two-high, one-low initiative, navigate through business or economic cycles, stay the course for the long run, and create lasting value. Next, let's invite our CFO, Ms.

Yan, to present the financial results and guidance.

Huiping Yan: Thank you, Chairman Lai, and thank you, Sophie. Hello to everyone on the call. As I walk through our financials, please note that unless specifically mentioned, all numbers quoted are in RMB, and percentage changes refer to year-over-year comparisons. Detailed information of our financial performance, unit economics, and cash flow are posted on our website, so here, I will only focus on some of the key highlights. In the third quarter, as industry competition continues to shift from price to value, we remained focused on profitable growth and higher-quality market share. Parcel volume grew 7% to 10.2 billion. Market share increased 0.7 percentage points to 20.1%. Total revenue rose 21% to CNY 14.4 billion.

Operating profit rose 23.8% to CNY 3 billion. Adjusted net income was CNY 2.6 billion, which grew 20.7% year-over-year after excluding a non-comparable CNY 376 million tax refund received in the third quarter last year, whereas such refund was received in the second quarter this year. ASP for the core express delivery rose CNY 0.16, or 13.7%, given improving product mix towards higher-value KA volume consisted fast-growing reverse logistics volume. Unit KA revenue increased CNY 0.17. Higher average parcel weight contributed CNY 0.01 gain, offsetting CNY 0.01 decline in other revenues. Total cost of revenue was CNY 10.8 billion, up 21.6%.

Overall unit cost for the core express delivery business rose 14.2%, or CNY 0.13, which included a CNY 0.15 increase in KA costs, and it was consistent with KA volume expansion. Despite pressure from the rise of oil prices, our combined unit sorting and transportation costs decreased by 2.8%, or CNY 0.02, thanks to continued digitization and lean ops initiatives. Breaking this down, unit line-haul transportation costs declined 5.8% to CNY 0.32. Our unit sorting costs remained flat at CNY 0.25. Gross profit increased 19.5% to CNY 3.5 billion, and gross margin rate was 24.6%, which contracted slightly by 0.3 percentage points. SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, decreased 5% to CNY 598 million.

As a percentage of revenue, SG&A excluding SBC declined to 4.2%. Income from operations rose 23.8% to CNY 3 billion, and our operating margin expanded by 0.4 percentage point to 20.7%. Operating cash flow was CNY 3.7 billion for the quarter, showing a 15.9% increase. Adjusted EBITDA rose 14.3% to CNY 4.1 billion. Capital expenditure for third quarter totaled CNY 1.3 billion, and we anticipated the full year CapEx to be around CNY 6 billion. For our outlook, based on current market and operating conditions, we are maintaining our previously guided full year 2026 parcel volume guidance to be 6%-10% growth year-over-year, or a total volume range of 40.83 billion-42.37 billion parcels.

These estimates reflect management's current preliminary view and remain subject to change. This concludes our prepared remarks. Operator, please open the line for questions. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please limit yourself to two questions. At this time, we will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. The first question comes from Aaron Luo with UBS. Please go ahead.

Aaron Luo: [Non-English content]. Thanks Mr. Lai, Ms. Yan, for taking my question. I have two. The first one is, how should we think about the slowdown in the industry volume growth, and what's your outlook for parcel volume, both for the sector and for ZTO in 4Q this year and next year? The second question is, how durable you think is the anti-involution discipline, and how do you see industry pricing evolving from here? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you, Aaron, for your question. Now let me translate and supplement where necessary. First of all, the express delivery industry has experienced high growth for many years, and now last year had reached 200 billion parcels. On such a high base, it is reasonable to understand the lower growth level. Second, we are in an economic cycle where high growth is not conducive. As anti-involution policies continue to take effect, we are seeing fewer lower-priced parcels, and the industry is moving towards a higher quality versus low price scale expansion. With all these drawbacks, ZTO's volume growth amidst the industry growth moderation, we are placing greater emphasis on winning higher quality market share.

In the third quarter, our parcel volume grew faster than the industry average. Our retail parcel grew 57% year-over-year, well ahead of our overall e-commerce parcel growth. We expect this trend to continue in the fourth quarter. Further, based on what we have seen so far this peak season, daily parcel volume for the industry seems to be less pronounced with peak that was seen in the past. Looking ahead, we expect slower volume growth to become the industry norm. We expect ZTO, however, to continue to grow faster than the industry by strengthening our differentiated service capabilities and capturing higher quality market share. Your second question.

We believe the anti-involution policy is designed to protect the interest of our outlets and couriers at the front line and to foster a healthy and orderly competitive environment. At its core, the policy seeks to discourage competition through below-cost pricing. The current round of measures reflected shared interests and support from both policymakers and industry participants, including outlets and couriers. Since its implementation, industry pricing and profitability have recovered meaningfully, while network stability has further improved. We view this policy as long-term and expect it to remain stable for the foreseeable future. Since the beginning of the campaign, the industry has shifted towards higher quality development. Price competition continues, yet it is becoming more and more rational overall.

Price softened in some markets during low season, yet entering into the peak season, prices have been recovering in key markets, including Yiwu and Hebei. As industry growth normalizes, we expect price competition to become more orderly, and the overall industry pricing practice will remain within a healthy range.

Operator: The next question comes from Qianlei Fan with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Qianlei Fan: [Non-English content]. Let me translate for myself. Good morning, Lai Zong, Yan Zong and Sophie. Thank you for taking my question and congratulations on a very robust operating level profit growth. I have two questions. The first question is related with reverse logistics. The company mentioned that retail parcels growth reached 57% in the quarter. Wondering what is the driver of the accelerated retail parcel growth in this quarter? Specifically want to check out of this retail parcels, how was the growth from the reverse logistics parcels, and is there any outlook related with its growth in next year? The second question is about the shareholder return.

The company mentioned under the current repurchase plan, there are still $1.1 billion not used. Wondering if there are any more detailed execution plan on the share repurchase? Also, over the mid to long term, is there any initial thoughts on how to fund our shareholder return? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question. Now, let me translate. The reverse logistics and including the retail parcel in our total KA volume is key component of our high-quality development strategy and it reflects the progress we have made in product and service diversification. It reflects our strength in improving quality, particularly in the last mile network to break away from homogenized competition. In the meantime, as we provide access to our courier, the first-hand market price so as to further incentivize them to spend the time and pick up retail parcels, it helped improve their earnings as well as provided motivation for them to improve quality of services, including responsiveness and on-time pickup.

Regarding the parcel profitability, the auction process by platform for reverse logistics has put some downward pressure on prices. Higher volume and refined cost control have partially offset that pressure. We are also expecting our individual retail parcel business, as stated earlier, to continue to grow. Both retail and reverse volume growth will continue to be supported by our overall initiatives to improve volume and at the same time improve profitability. Regarding the shareholder return, since the issuance of our buyback CB in February, we have continued to execute our share repurchase plan. Year-to-date, we have repurchased approximately $1.05 billion of shares.

The total amount allocated to repurchase under this program is $1.4 billion, equal to the net proceeds of the offering. We will complete the remaining repurchase as market condition permits. We expect the amount spent on share repurchase this year to exceed 100% of last year's net profit. Accordingly, we will not pay an additional dividend this year. We will resume our standing return program for 2026 program, return profit to shareholders under which total annual shareholder return will be no less than 50% of the previous year's net profit, taking into consideration our free cash and profit level. Hope that answers your question.

Operator: Thank you. The next question comes from Steve Qiu with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Steve Qiu: [Non-English content]. Thank you. My first question is about social insurance and whether it could become a driver of industry pricing improvement. So recently, the peers in logistics sector and other companies in the ADR space have all raised the issue of social insurance compliance. So we have noticed that ZTO's disclosed contribution remains ahead of the franchise-based models peers. So could management comment on whether we currently stand on social insurance contribution for the headquarters employees as well as the franchisee employees? And if the compliance improves further, could that become a driver of industry-wide price increases?

My second question is about balancing the volume share as well as the profit when demand is soft and capacities remains relatively ample. So with demand weakening as well as e-commerce coming under pressure while industry capacities still abundant, how does management think about the trade-off between parcel volume share and profitability going into the future? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question, Steve. First of all, as it relates to the social insurance, there is growing attention to how the rights of express delivery personnel are protected. A multi-tiered social security system designed for different labor type is gradually taking shape with broader insurance and occupational injury coverage. Together with anti-involution policies, these efforts aim to standardize employment practices, raise compliance standards across the industry, and encourages operators to compete on service quality. The policy is being rolled out step by step with different arrangements depending on employment status. Workers with formal employment relationships, such as those employed by ZTO brand and platform, participate in social insurance as required by law.

Occupational injury coverage is also gradually expanding to cover workers in flexible work arrangements. This gives the industry time to make an orderly transition. Since the founding of our business, we have upheld our core philosophy of shared success. Our network partners and frontline couriers have always been essential to our network success. In managing our own workforce, we continue to strengthen our employment practices and protect the rights of frontline workers. In line with the postal regulations guidance, we also support our network partners in meeting the applicable social security requirements gradually. We embrace the changes that are necessary.

In the near term, the rollout will put some pressure on per parcel cost, and it is an issue faced by all industry participants equally. As you mentioned, potentially if price increase is one of the key solutions to maintain order of the industry growth, we will benefit from that as well. Over the medium to longer term, stable coverage will help strengthen network stability, reduce courier turnover, and improve last mile service quality. That is great for the entire industry. ZTO will continue to stay at the forefront of the industry and support its transition to higher quality development.

The second question relating to balancing volume share in face of ample capacity, what are the trade-offs between shares and volume? As the anti-involution policy continues to take effect, there's less room to gain additional volume through price alone. Service quality, cost control, and ability to operate a network efficiently are becoming increasingly important. Competition, we expect the differences among industry players to be more pronounced in those leading companies with strength in all three areas are well positioned to gain higher quality markets. ZTO has always been committed to a sustainable long-term mindset rather than pursuing short-term growth through temporary volume expansion.

For us, high-quality development comes down to clear priorities, outlets become steadily more profitable, couriers' income continuing to rise, and our operations staying healthy and efficient overall. Our strategy continues to focus on higher quality services, higher quality market share, and lower cost end-to-end. This has been the strategy consistently carried out throughout the growth of our business, and we will continue to build around differentiated service capabilities, advancing end-to-end lean operations, strengthen our network, and supporting our frontline partners. As we maintain our leadership in parcel volume, we will aim to improve quality of our market share while maintaining healthy profitability. We believe this will further expand our competitive advantage over medium and longer term.

Looking ahead, as we stated that we want to develop ourselves to be a comprehensive logistic service provider, all the installed base will be multi-used to meet the market demands. As we see beyond e-commerce logistics, we are better prepared and well-positioned to serve manufacturing, agriculture, as well as specialty logistic capabilities. The trade-off perhaps is not necessarily going to be different. We seek higher quality, seek higher quality volume share, as well as healthy profitable growth. Hope that answers your question.

Operator: Thank you. The next question comes from Gangxian Liu with CICC. Please go ahead.

Gangxian Liu: [Non-English content]. Let me translate for myself. Thank you for taking my question. First, congrats on the company's solid performance on the core business. My question is about the cost. We observed that per parcel transportation costs fell year-on-year on Q3 despite higher oil price, while per parcel sorting costs stayed flat. Could management break down and explain the drivers behind this? For the fourth quarter outlook, will oil price still be a pressure? What hedging measures do we have in place if the situation continues into next year? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question. In the third quarter, rising fuel prices continued to put pressure on transportation costs. It increased the per parcel transportation costs by approximately CNY 0.01. Nevertheless, thanks to the further implementation of digitization and smart tools, as well as improved lean process management, combined per-parcel transportation and sorting costs still declined by CNY 0.02 compared to last year. Specifically, transportation cost in the third quarter, the cost per parcel was CNY 0.32, down CNY 0.02 from last year. On the reduction side, first, our proprietary intelligent dispatch system adjusts vehicle schedules, route, and capacity matching in real time as parcel flows changes.

This helps us to improve load rates, reduce unused capacity, and avoid unnecessary mileages. Second, we have continued to strengthen fleet management. We have established our standard cost models for vehicle operations and maintenance, introduced tiered incentives based on load rates, and rewarded drivers for cost savings. These measures have helped us bringing in fleet operation and maintenance costs, bringing up the operational efficiency and maintain costs down further. On the fuel prices, diesel price have remained volatile since the second quarter amid international environmental development.

However, diesel price added approximately CNY 0.01 to transportation cost per parcel in the third quarter, and we expect a similar, or if not a little bit more, level of impact in the fourth quarter. We are taking two steps to manage this pressure. First, we continue to expand our fleet of natural gas trucks and have begun testing electrical vehicles on selected routes. Second, we will be utilizing our in-house fuel stations to secure better diesel supply. On sorting, in the third quarter, sorting cost per parcel was CNY 0.25, flat year-over-year. Higher depreciation and amortization expenses associated with newly commissioned facilities put pressure on unit costs.

However, these increases were offset by improvements in facility automation and labor productivity. Specifically, on the equipment front, we continue to invest in smart equipment at our sorting centers and upgrade and retrofit some of the aging equipment to improve efficiency. On the labor front, we also leverage digital tools to optimize shift scheduling, refine position-based performance assessment, and enhance our training and incentive program to keep improving labor productivity.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Huiping Yan, the CFO, for any closing remarks.

Huiping Yan: Thanks again for everybody joining us for the call, and thank you for your questions. We are looking forward to further discuss with you, if any other questions could not be asked during this time. We thank you for your support, and we look forward to speaking with you again soon.

Operator: The conference has now concluded. Thank you for attending today's presentation. You may now disconnect.

#2976. It’s Official: Anthropic Prices Its IPO at $83 a Share. Here’s What We Know (and What We Don’t)

Anthropic’s IPO was priced above its range, and the final raise could rival SpaceX’s record deal.

By Matt Frankel, CFP® – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:17PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models, priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, according to Reuters, Bloomberg and CNBC, which all cited people familiar with the matter. That's well above the $70-$78 range the company set when it launched its roadshow last week.

Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. Pricing above the range is a strong sign of demand and sets up one of the largest IPOs on record, as well as the first from a major developer of frontier AI models.

Anthropic originally planned to sell 825 million shares, about 801 million of which would be offered by the company and the remainder from existing shareholders. At $83 apiece, that share count alone would raise about $68.5 billion. Anthropic also lined up a $26 billion private placement with major chip, cloud, and software companies, bringing the combined total to more than $94 billion. And at $83 per share, Anthropic would be valued at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

SpaceX (SPCX +1.27%) set the IPO record in June, raising $75 billion by selling about 555.6 million shares at $135 each. Including the extra shares sold to underwriters, the total came to about $86.2 billion. At its original share count, Anthropic's IPO would come in slightly below SpaceX's base deal, but it would require only about 10% more shares to match it. With the private placement included, Anthropic's total fundraising would already top what SpaceX raised.

A few important details aren't official yet. Bloomberg and Reuters both reported that Anthropic was likely to upsize the offering (sell more shares than originally planned), but Anthropic hasn't disclosed how many shares it's selling. Until it does, we don't know the final amount raised, whether this becomes the largest IPO ever, or the exact valuation. We also don't know whether the underwriters will buy additional shares or where the stock will open on Thursday. As with many hot IPO stocks, the first trade could come well above $83.
